items.loreDesc: A traveller's flask, dented flat on one side. Empty, but it still smells faintly of something strong.

loreStory.t: Everything else that comes down off a
Nightmule

is work — rope, harness links, canvas, a knife for rations. The flask is the only thing in that load that was not about getting somewhere. It is dented flat down one whole side and the cap still seats, so it took the blow while it was full and did not lose a drop, which is a good flask, and the man who owned it knew that about it.
Wendell

is clear on what the object is for. Nobody carries a flask to drink by himself, he says. You carry it so that at the end of a wet day you have something to hand across, and the handing is the point and the drink is only the excuse. He says this at a fire, in exchange for company, which is a man describing his own method and trusting you not to notice. Twenty-five gold, and he has never once been asked for a demonstration.

items.name: Dry Grass
items.description: Olive stalks tied off with cord — fodder for a farm that is gone. Sorrel still hauls its share to the gate.
items.loreDesc: Olive stalks tied off with cord, dry to the heart. Fodder, thatch, bedding — and the best tinder on the road.
loreStory: Ask three people what it is for and get fodder, thatch and bedding. Ask anyone who keeps a fire and get one answer. A twist of it rides inside the coat, against the body, where it stays dry through whatever the sky is doing; it comes out last, it goes under the kindling, and it is the difference between a lit hearth at dusk and a cold one.

loreStory.t: There is a girl on one of the western rotas — one of the few
still kept

— who let hers get wet at a ford and walked four hours back for another twist rather than come in and say so. She was fourteen when she died. She has kept that fire ninety years and she is still fourteen, and the walk back is what the other keepers tell about her, in the tone people use for somebody they intend to be proud of forever.

items.name: Rune Locket
items.description: Oval bronze, knotted with spirals nobody reads aloud twice. The Palehusk wore it under skin that was not its own.
items.loreDesc: Oval bronze, knotted over with spirals, a ring at the top for a cord. It is a locket. It has never once opened.
loreStory: Opening it is the first thing everybody tries and the last thing anybody manages. Some have a hinge line under the knotwork and some have no hinge line whatsoever, and all of them are shut, and the trade has been quiet about that for a long while, on the grounds that eighty-five gold is a fair price and the question is not worth losing over.

loreStory.t: Two facts sit side by side in
the Chronicle
with no third fact between them. They come up in the grass where
Runemane
walks. And they come off the black rock, grown in under the chest skin of a
Palehusk
— a thing with nothing at all inside it, carrying, over the exact place a heart would sit, a container that has never been opened.

items.name: Ember Shard
items.description: Leaf-shaped crystal veined orange and red. It stays warm in the pouch, like the shell it was prised from.
items.loreDesc: Leaf-shaped crystal veined orange and red. It stays warm in the pouch, like the shell it was prised from.
loreStory: Blood heat, near enough, and it keeps it for years. That makes it the one piece of junk with an obvious use and no cleverness required: it goes in a pocket, and the pocket is warm.

loreStory.t: Jehanne

buys them by the sack every autumn — the cracked and cloudy ones, which is why she can afford sacks — and hands them out on the winter rounds to whoever is sitting up at a fire with no one else on the rota. She says nothing over them. She has nothing to say over them. An old man at the third fire thanked her last year for the blessing, and she stood a moment, and then told him he was welcome, because correcting him would have cost him something and saved her nothing at all.

items.name: Oyster Shell
items.description: One half of a fossil bivalve, chalk on the outside, pearly within. The dunes are full of dead seas.
items.loreDesc: One half of a fossil bivalve, chalk on the outside, pearly within. The dunes are full of dead seas.

loreStory.t: They come up as halves. A woman on the south dune camps spent two years looking for the other half of hers — not a similar one, the one, hinge-notch and all — and she went at it properly: every shell and flake that came in off a
delver
's wake laid against her own on a folded cloth, a tally kept, a small fee paid for the privilege of looking.

loreStory: She found one that fitted. It was not the mate; the chalk was wrong and the size a shade under. It closed anyway, and sat closed in her hand, and she stopped that evening and has not started again. She still buys shells off anyone coming in off the sand. She does not lay them against anything now. She says she likes the noise they make in the bag.

items.name: Wild Herbs
items.description: A fistful of green stalks pulled up roots and all, tied at the base by somebody in a hurry.
items.loreDesc: A fistful of green stalks pulled up roots and all, tied at the base by somebody in a hurry.

loreStory.t: There is a pot on at every fire worth the name, and this is most of what goes in it: whatever came up green within a short walk, pulled roots and all, tied with whatever the picker had on them. Nobody arrives hungry. That is not what the pot is for. It is for the hour after
a waking

, when a person has been told what has happened to them, and asked their name, and cannot produce it yet, and needs something to do with their hands while they try. One man got as far as saying his mother put nettles in everything and it made the whole house smell like a wet field. That was his one true thing. His name came back three days later, and of the two it was much the smaller.

items.name: Frost Claw
items.description: A blue-grey claw with rime still on the edge. Bergclaw leaves them in shields, mostly other people's.
items.loreDesc: A blue-grey claw with rime still on the edge. Bergclaw leaves them in shields, mostly other people's.

loreStory.t: Lay one flat and the curve very nearly closes on itself. That is not a claw for opening a thing — that is a hook, and a hook is for holding on. Shields that come back with one in them come back with the boards pulled rather than scored: the arm took hold and leaned, and whoever was behind it had about a second to decide whether to keep the shield. They almost all keep it.
Osric

has re-boarded eight in two years and keeps the claws in a jar on the sill, still cold, still rimed, sweating a ring into the wood. He offers them back and is told no every time, by people who cannot say why either. He has stopped asking. He has not thrown one out.

items.name: Frost Star
items.description: A six-armed crystal that never quite melts. Winterfang's mane grows them and drops them behind it.
items.loreDesc: A six-armed crystal that never quite melts. Winterfang's mane grows them and drops them behind it.
loreStory: Never quite is the whole of it. A dropped star loses a hair's width a year and no more, so a trail of them is a trail with dates on it: big ones from this winter, smaller from the winter before, back and back until you are reading a line the animal walked a century ago and can still put your thumb on.

loreStory.t: Gunnar

measures those lines, because they are the only straight thing this country hands out free. He has one off the north fells, eighty stars long, and the far half of it does not lie where the near half points. The ground under it moved. He wrote the numbers down and has shown them to no one, and when
Winterfang
comes up at a fire he talks about the cold instead.

items.name: Beast Claw
items.description: One dark claw with the fur still on the knuckle. It came off a paw the size of a dinner plate.
items.loreDesc: One dark claw with the fur still on the knuckle. It came off a paw the size of a dinner plate.

loreStory.t: Two things in the west leave a claw this size, and only one of them ever grew hair. Scrape the knuckle: coarse brown, flattened all one way, skin still on underneath. That is
Mireback
, which was an ordinary bear on ordinary ground before the water came up over its round. The other kind leaves grit and green crumbs and no hair at all, because
Cragback
was never an animal — it is a hill a hundred valleys agreed on, and hills do not grow coats.

loreStory: Buyers on the west road pay double for hair. It is not a better claw — same socket, same edge. What the extra gold buys is the certainty that the paw had a bear inside it once, which matters enormously to some people and not at all to others, and both sorts drink at the same fire and gave up arguing about it years ago.

items.name: Gilded Fang
items.description: Someone gilded a hunter's tooth, hollow at the root and polished bright. Nobody asks whose mouth it left.
items.loreDesc: Someone gilded a hunter's tooth, hollow at the root and polished bright. Nobody asks whose mouth it left.

loreStory.t: The leaf costs more than the tooth under it, and that is the exercise, not an accident of taste.
Gold

is the one substance every century remembers the same way, which is why a coin holds while everything around it goes soft, and there are people who reason from that fact straight to this practice: lay enough of it over a thing and the thing comes along for the ride. It has never been properly tested. It is done anyway, and it is not done to wedding rings or lucky coins. It is done to teeth. This one went over a
Duskfang

's, out of an age so far back it has stopped coming up at the fires at all — which is the part worth sitting with, because gilding is what a person does about a creature when they have run out of anybody willing to talk about it. Seventy-two gold, and most of that is the gold.

items.name: Husked Nuts
items.description: Hard glossy kernels streaked tan and brown, a good fistful. Small woodland things hoard them, and now so do you.
items.loreDesc: Hard glossy kernels streaked tan and brown, a good fistful. Small woodland things hoard them, and now so do you.
loreStory: Hard as a knuckle. There are two ways to open one — a flat stone, or your own back teeth — and which a person reaches for tells you how long they have been here.

loreStory.t: The newly woken

protect their teeth. They will not say why, and the reason is a chair in a bright room and a mother who was firm about it. Everyone else cracks them on the molars without a thought, because a tooth here is a remembered tooth and behaves like the rest of you. The first time somebody hears their own jaw go through a shell and feels nothing whatever about it, they generally go quiet for the rest of the evening, and the fire lets them, and somebody moves the bowl within reach. Five gold the fistful. That is the cost of the fistful, and it is not the price.

items.name: Ember Dust
items.description: A handful of grit that still glows in the palm. Cinderhowl leaves a trail of it wherever it walks.
items.loreDesc: A handful of grit that still glows in the palm. Cinderhowl leaves a trail of it wherever it walks.

loreStory.t: Twenty-four gold the twist, and there is one reason for the price: a pinch of it under wet kindling gives you a fire when nothing else in the pack will. In the rain country that is not a convenience. A night with no fire is a night with no telling in it, and the walkers up there buy by the tin. The woman who supplies most of the west road quotes all of that back at you while she weighs, and she has her own arithmetic. She works after dark, a hundred paces behind
the burning dog

, sweeping the grit out of the ruts before it goes out — twelve years of it, one road, both directions. Every fire between the ford and the high fields is lit off her sweepings. She has never sat at one.

items.name: Mandrake
items.description: A knobbly root with legs of its own and a wilted crown. The Stumpling was carrying it, or it was family.
items.loreDesc: A knobbly root with legs of its own and a wilted crown. The Stumpling was carrying it, or it was family.

loreStory.t: Forty gold for a root off a
Stumpling

's foot, and every coin of it is the shape. The stalls grade them the way a fishmonger grades fish. Two legs is a root. Two legs and arms is a good root. A head — a knob with a fold in it, the light doing the rest — is a price you have to ask about, quietly, and the seller takes his time answering.

loreStory: It sells as a joke. They hang it by the crown with a scrap of coat on it and do the voice, and the crowd obliges. It is bought in earnest far more often than the stalls admit, by people careful to be laughing while they pay. There is a right way to sell a man a root shaped like a small person: take his gold, make the joke, wrap it well, and do not watch him leave.

items.name: Gold Ore
items.description: Rubble-grade rock studded with raw gold. It was a Mosscairn's shoulder until you argued about ownership.
items.loreDesc: Rubble-grade rock studded with raw gold. It was a Mosscairn's shoulder until you argued about ownership.
loreStory: The first thing a new cracker is taught about ore is how to be disappointed properly. Teeth are no use on rock. You drag a fleck across a pale stone and read the line it leaves — true gold draws yellow, the pretty fraud draws black — and then you heft the lump, because a fist of real ore weighs like a bigger stone than it looks.

loreStory.t: The second thing is that
Halvard
pays under weight for it, always, and will not be moved.
A coin is the one thing everyone remembers the same

; a rock with gold in it is a rock with an argument in it, and he does not trade in arguments. Melt it and come back, he says. Half the sheds think he is squeezing them. The other half has noticed he pays exactly the same under-weight to the people he likes.

items.name: Amber Fang
items.description: Broad amber-yellow tooth, split from crown to root. Even an Emberjaw loses one on the wrong kind of bone.
items.loreDesc: Broad amber-yellow tooth, split from crown to root. Even an Emberjaw loses one on the wrong kind of bone.
loreStory: It split crown to root, and it split from closing, not from being struck. A tooth that comes apart the long way did it to itself, biting down on something that would not open.

loreStory.t: Which is why there is a list, and the list is the whole conversation every time one of these crosses a counter.
Ironhide
's plates. The black glass out of the volcano. Whatever it is a
Palemaw

keeps working on ground where nothing else will feed. Three, and everyone agrees on the three, and then the counting runs on a beat too long, and somebody buys the fang, and the talk goes somewhere else.

loreStory: Thirty gold. Amber ivory takes a shine like nothing else in the trade, and half the buyers do not care about any of the above, which is a mercy on the ones who do.

items.name: Great Fang
items.description: A fang as long as a hand, worn blunt at the tip. Tuskmaul has broken plenty on other people's shields.
items.loreDesc: A fang as long as a hand, worn blunt at the tip. Tuskmaul has broken plenty on other people's shields.

loreStory.t: Buyers want them blunt, and the reasoning is not sentiment. A fang worn round at the point has been in service a long time, which means the animal carrying it is old and settled and accounted for, standing where it has stood since before anyone thought to look — the way
the old bull
stands. A sharp one has come off something that has not finished growing.

loreStory: So the blunt fetches thirty-two gold and the sharp fetches half, and the difference has nothing to do with ivory. It is the arithmetic. Somewhere in country that everybody has agreed for two hundred years is empty, on ground people cross without looking up, there is a new one. The man who brings a sharp fang to a counter is asked where he found it, politely, immediately, and by everybody in the room at once.

items.name: Jade Shard
items.description: Teal-green crystal with a wicked point, prised out of a Mosscairn's seams. Holds an edge and a grudge.
items.loreDesc: Teal-green crystal with a wicked point, prised out of a Mosscairn's seams. Holds an edge and a grudge.
loreStory: The grudge is a shop joke. A hafted jade point keeps its edge past all reason — past the steel beside it on the bench, past the arm using it — and when a cutler cannot explain a thing he gives it a temper instead. So the shards are surly, the good ones are spiteful, and everybody laughs.

loreStory.t: An apprentice at the sheds asked, in front of the whole bench, whether a piece off a
Mosscairn

remembers having been part of one. The bench laughed. The master did not. He let it go all afternoon, and then, while the boy was sweeping up, said without turning round that they do not ask that in here, and went back to work.

items.name: Emerald
items.description: Deep green and sharply faceted, prised out of stubborn rock. Mosscairn keeps them in its shoulders.
items.loreDesc: Deep green and sharply faceted, prised out of stubborn rock. Mosscairn keeps them in its shoulders.

loreStory.t: Beautiful and structurally useless. Emerald is full of its own flaws and every one of them is a line waiting to be asked a question; set it in a blade and the first honest blow finds one.
Sigrun

will take your money for the work and tell you plainly where it is going: handle, never head. A stone in the head takes every blow you strike for as long as you own the thing. A stone in the handle takes only what your own hand gives it. She has never once elaborated on the distinction, and the apprentices who have looked closely at the head of her hammer have never asked her to.

items.name: Herb Bundle
items.description: Long green stalks tied into a sheaf, damp from the ditch some blob had been squatting in.
items.loreDesc: Long green stalks tied into a sheaf, damp from the ditch some blob had been squatting in.
loreStory: Nine people at one fire, nine names for it, every one of them certain. Marsh-tongue. Ditch-sorrel. Goosegrass, poor-man's-bay, the one the drovers call cutfinger, and a Latin one from a man who was a physician for thirty years and has not been one for four hundred. They agreed on exactly two things: boil it, and it is good with fish.

loreStory.t: Bettany

wrote down all nine, which annoyed the entire fire, since eight of them are obviously wrong. She will not choose. Her position, stated once and never repeated, is that a plant nine people remember nine ways is a plant nine people are holding up, and
the book
is not in the business of taking eight of them away. The stall on that road sells it under the name everyone actually uses, which is bundle.

items.name: Jewel Beetle
items.description: A beetle in green and blue enamel, legs folded neat. Too handsome to squash, too dead to object.
items.loreDesc: A beetle in green and blue enamel, legs folded neat. Too handsome to squash, and in no position to object.

loreStory.t: The shell does not dull and does not fade, which makes it the brooch of anybody who cannot afford a brooch. Pinned at the throat it reads as enamel from four feet, and only the very rude look closer.
Osric

bought one last spring for a birthday, which is a thing almost nobody here keeps any more — he still counts in living years and marks the date the way he marked it before. He was two months out. He gave it anyway, and it is being worn.

items.name: Ooze Glob
items.description: A palmful of green ooze that keeps its shape and none of its dignity. Alchemists take it by the jar.
items.loreDesc: A palmful of green ooze that keeps its shape and none of its dignity. Alchemists take it by the jar.

loreStory.t: Sold by the jar, and the jar is the argument.
Seven gold

buys a jar of it, so the only thing left to haggle over is whose jar, and every buyer on the fen road keeps one that is a finger taller than everybody else's and swears it is the standard. There is a woman working the low crossings with her own on a strap, fired to a scratched line she put there herself, who will not pour into anything but that. She has been called a great deal at that counter. She has also never once been short-paid, so half the crossing brings her their globs now and lets her do the pouring, and she takes nothing for it. She is not doing it for them. She is doing it at him.

items.name: Green Scales
items.description: A patch of overlapping green scales, still faintly damp. Palemaw sheds them in the cave shallows.
items.loreDesc: A patch of overlapping green scales, still faintly damp. Palemaw sheds them in the cave shallows.

loreStory.t: There is a shelter at the last fire before the black rock: four stone walls roofed in green scale, a handful at a time, over years. Everybody who works that ground adds to it on the way out. Overlapped right, the scales throw rain off like slate and never crack in the heat coming off the rock, and they never dry either — the ceiling is damp all night, which is the only complaint anyone makes. Twelve gold a patch and hundreds up there: the roof is worth more than the shelter and the woodpile together, and it has never been stripped. Not sentiment. Anybody stripping it would have to carry it out past the men who put it up, and they are all coming back the same way, off
Palemaw
's ground, in a hurry.

items.name: Green Slime
items.description: Half a pond-dweller, domed and translucent, still faintly warm. Alchemists want it and will not say why.
items.loreDesc: Half a pond-dweller, domed and translucent, still faintly warm. Alchemists want it and will not say why.

loreStory.t: Boiled two hours it goes down to a thin green size that holds paper to paper and does not turn brittle, and that is what
Bettany
binds
the Chronicle
with. Every account of the worst day of somebody's life that she has ever taken down is held into the spine by eight gold of pond-dweller off a fen stall.

loreStory: She explained this once, at the stall, in detail, being a scribe and unable to help it. The price was eleven inside the month. She has explained nothing at a market since, buys by the sack now, and lets the road go on believing she is one of the alchemists — which is cheaper, and, she admits, a better story than the truth.

items.name: Green Eye
items.description: A green eye with a black slit, still bright. Mireglare's stare goes out of it about an hour after death.
items.loreDesc: A green eye with a black slit, still bright. Mireglare's stare stays in it about an hour, then goes out.
loreStory: It is the one thing on the stall you can price by looking at it. Bright, twenty-eight. Dull, eight. The hour in between is the entire difference, so sellers come off the crossing at a trot with the bag held level and quote you the time they cut it.

loreStory.t: A walker out of the low ford keeps one long past its hour, flat and grey now, in a pouch he does not sell out of.
The cat that comes into firelight

looked him over one night — the whole way, chin up, as you are supposed to let it — and then moved on to the next face and out into the dark. He has had a good many years to decide whether being passed over is the good outcome and has not managed it. He keeps the eye because he would like to be able to ask it.

items.name: Rock Pile
items.description: Rounded brown stones in a heap, which is all a Mosscairn amounts to once the magic stops holding it together.
items.loreDesc: Rounded brown stones in a heap, which is all a Mosscairn amounts to once it stops holding itself together.

loreStory.t: Three. Not three each — three for the heap, and the heap weighs about what you do. So the money in rubble is not in the taking, it is in the carrying, and behind every crew there are men who have never
opened a shape

in their lives and make a steady living hauling other people's stone to the weighing-post at the road. There is one on the east road who has done it forty years. To anyone who calls it a poor trade he points out that he is paid per stone the same as the man who took it, sleeps a good deal better, and has never in all that time carried anything off a hillside except the weight.

items.name: Sage Leaves
items.description: Bitter grey-green leaves off the meadow scrub. Good in stew, better in poultices, fatal by the handful.
items.loreDesc: Bitter grey-green leaves off the meadow scrub. Good in stew, better in a poultice, and a handful will put you down.

loreStory.t: The women who sell it count the leaves into your hand out loud. That is not ceremony. Three in a pot of stew is a good dinner. A dozen crushed into a wet rag is the best thing going for a bad shoulder. A fistful, chewed, and you go down — properly down, on your face, in the road — and come back together beside the nearest fire some hours later,
the way anyone does
, pockets intact, a hole where your evening was, and a little less of whatever you had been thinking about.

loreStory: One man worked that out and made a habit of it. Pleasant, paid without haggling, back every few weeks and lighter each time. The trade argued about him for a winter and came out with a rule it keeps still: they will sell you your fistful. They will not sell you the second, they will not say who might, and every woman on that road knows his face.

items.name: Iron Chain
items.description: Three pitted iron links, worn smooth where a harness rubbed. The Nightmule that wore it is still out there.
items.loreDesc: Three pitted iron links, worn smooth where a harness rubbed. The Nightmule that wore it is still out there.

loreStory.t: There is a carter at the east crossing who pays nine gold a set for these and is not melting them. He is rebuilding the rig. He has the breeching, most of a collar, a bridle with one cheekpiece, a pad — all of it picked up off the ground behind
the mule that still keeps its route

— and he is short two trace chains and a hame strap. Ask what he means to do with a finished harness and he will tell you flatly: put it on. Not to stop the animal. It has never minded being touched, and it has never once stopped. He wants to load it, and walk at its head, and be the voice up front, since the voice it halts for is not coming.
Wendell
has offered to name him the stops on the old road. He says he will take that when the rig is done.

items.name: Long Bone
items.description: One heavy leg bone, clean at both ends. Gravecharger is missing several and has not noticed.
items.loreDesc: One heavy leg bone, clean at both ends. Gravecharger is missing several and has not noticed.
loreStory: Seven gold, and the glue you boil out of it is worth more than the bone, which is the first economics anybody in this trade learns and about the only lesson that sticks. Two days at a rolling simmer, skim, reduce, cool it to a slab: the size that holds a haft to a head and a bow to itself.

loreStory.t: Osric

buys them by the sack and complains about the smell in the same words every time, which the whole smithy can now say along with him. He has costed it twice and found both times he would do better buying glue ready-made. He boils bones anyway, on the grounds that a smith who buys everything he uses is a shopkeeper. Ask what he does with the difference and he changes the subject, because he is putting it by in
gold
, and does not know what for, and has not for two years.

items.name: Hooked Wing
items.description: Leathery brown membrane on finger-bones, with a claw at the crown. Whatever flies on these keeps to its cave.
items.loreDesc: Leathery brown membrane on finger-bones, with a claw at the crown. Whatever flies on these keeps to its cave.

loreStory.t: Look at the hook, not the wing. The inner curve is polished — not scuffed, polished, the way a stair rail goes under sixty years of the same hand — which means the animal hangs, and hangs in one place, often enough to wear horn smooth against rock. Somewhere there is a ceiling with a groove worn into it. A cracker worked all that out over a winter, was extremely pleased with himself, and carried the wing east to put it to
Hearn

, who has been inside the only cave anyone means when they say the cave. Hearn turned it over twice, looked at the polish rather than the claw, said not that one, and handed it back. Twenty-two gold, and the wing is the cheap half of what you are buying. The rest is a room nobody has found.

items.name: Nacre Shard
items.description: Turn this flake of shell and it shifts green to violet. The dune gave it up; whatever grew it is long fossil.
items.loreDesc: Turn this flake of shell and it shifts green to violet. The dune gave it up; whatever grew it is long fossil.

loreStory.t: The broken edge is not one thing. It is about four hundred things, stacked: layer on layer on layer, each one a season of some flat, patient animal adding a little more house. That is all the colour is. Not a pigment — a count. Green going to violet is what four hundred years of doing the same small job, once a year, does to daylight coming through it. The water it worked in has been gone from that country since before anyone woke there. The sand turned its back plate up in a clean hollow behind a
delver
, and somebody dropped it in a bag with eleven other flakes and walked on, and it is worth sixty gold. The patient are not paid at a better rate than anyone else.

items.name: Ivory Talon
items.description: Cream-white and curved to a needle point, the socket left ragged. Glowbones and Frostwraiths grow them in sets.
items.loreDesc: Cream-white and curved to a needle point, the socket left ragged. Glowbones and Frostwraiths grow them in sets.
loreStory: Bore out the ragged end, bind it into a haft, and you have the best awl in the country: a point that goes through four thicknesses of hide and does not blunt, ever, however much of it you do. Every sail-mender, harness-maker and tent-patcher on the northern rounds is sewing with one. They cost more than the tools they replace, and the people who use them do not haggle.

loreStory.t: Where they come from is the part the trade steps around. There is a boy who walks the low edge of the high snow, picking them out of the drift where a
Frostwraith

has been working, and he brings down a dozen at a time. He will not say how far up he goes. The answer is plain enough to anyone who has been. No one at that fire asks him, and several of them are sewing while they do not ask.

items.name: Jade Amulet
items.description: A green disc with a pale gem set dead centre. Temple work, and Runemane still guards a heap of it.
items.loreDesc: A green disc with a pale gem set dead centre. Temple work, and Runemane still guards a heap of it.

loreStory.t: Eighty gold, and it moves faster than anything else off that field, for the plainest reason in the trade: it is the only piece of the place a person can wear.
The cogs
are a curiosity.
The little folded figures
unsettle people. This is a green disc with a stone in the middle, it hangs well, it does not chip, and you can put it on.

loreStory: So a lot of them are on. Count round any decent fire on the eastern road and you will find two or three, and their owners will tell you, correctly, that it is temple work, and that is the end of what any of them knows. Whatever the hall was for, whatever was said in it, whatever a person was undertaking while wearing one of these — that went with the walls. The disc came through. The trade priced it and passed it along, and there is not one person left who could tell the wearers whether they are allowed to.

items.name: Great Pearl
items.description: One flawless sphere, off-white with a lilac sheen. Nobody will say which water it was brought up out of.
items.loreDesc: One flawless sphere, off-white with a lilac sheen. Nobody will say which water it was brought up out of.
loreStory: Gold buys goods. A pearl is what you put on the table when the thing you want is not for sale, and at a hundred and ten it is well clear of the price of anything a person actually needs.

loreStory.t: A man set one down in front of
Bettany
and asked her to leave a name out of
the Chronicle

. Not his own. She did not take it and she did not argue with him. She wrote the offer down instead — the date, the sphere, the lilac in it, what it would have fetched, and the fact that a man had believed the book was the sort of thing that could be bought, which she noted was the more interesting half of the evening. She left his name out. That part he did get.

items.name: Fern Fronds
items.description: A fan of thick green fronds, snapped off at the stem. Sporehorn walks through whole banks of them.
items.loreDesc: One frond still furled tight, layered like a fist, already going gold along the outer edge.

loreStory.t: Hearn

keeps one in a cup of water on a sill and turns the cup a quarter every morning. He came back from the mountain alone and will not give one word about the inside. He will talk about the fern to anybody, at length, given the smallest opening.

loreStory: Cut furled, it goes on. That is the trick and the whole price — an hour later it has opened on the stem and it is a leaf, quite pretty, worth nothing. His opened in the cup over nine days, one turn at a time. By the sixth people were putting their heads round the door to look. By the eighth there were too many of them in the room and someone had carried a chair up. Very little here gets bigger. Nobody says that out loud, and a fern in a cup says it for them, and every one of them went home fed.

items.name: Lichen Rock
items.description: A fist of rock crusted in orange lichen. Cragback is made of these, and misses each one when it goes.
items.loreDesc: A fist of rock crusted in grey-green lichen. Cragback is made of these, and misses each one when it goes.

loreStory.t: The lichen is a clock. It wants forty still years to come in that thick, and a face that has just lost a stone is bare — so the pale patches on a
Cragback
are a robbery ledger, readable from the next ridge and dated by how far the green has crept back over them.

loreStory: Which is how the trade found out the thing it does not repeat at fires. A well-robbed one is slower. Take enough off a hillside and the hillside labours, so the crews go back to the animals they have already opened, because those are the easy ones, and they keep going back, and the bare faces spread. A crusted fist of rock fetches eight. A day's walk out and a day's walk back, for eight.

items.name: Thread Spool
items.description: Half a spool of plain linen thread. Something stitched the Palehusk together, and it was not a tailor.
items.loreDesc: Half a spool of plain linen thread. Something stitched the Palehusk together, and it was not a tailor.

loreStory.t: Dealers will tell you what the sewing on
the walking things

was for. They are guessing. The spool is the interesting part: every one that has ever come in off the black rock is half used, and ask ten people who have handled one to describe it and you get the same half, down to the tail of thread hanging loose at the side.

loreStory: A woman at a fire on the north road took hers in payment two winters ago and has mended out of it since — eleven coats, a tent wall, a boot she had no business saving. It is exactly as full as the day she got it. She stopped mentioning that at about the fourth coat, because of how people's faces went. She has not stopped sewing, and she would like it on record, if anybody is keeping one, that she got eleven coats out of a thing the rest of them were afraid to touch.

items.name: Loose Teeth
items.description: Molars, curved fangs and small incisors, no two from the same jaw. Palemaws and Emberjaws shed them constantly.
items.loreDesc: Molars, curved fangs and small incisors, no two from the same jaw. Palemaws and Emberjaws shed them constantly.
loreStory: Eight gold the mixed lot, and the mixing is the trade's teaching tool. Somebody tips a bag out on a cloth at a fire, the new ones go round the ring naming each tooth to its animal, whoever gets one wrong stands the next drink. It is a good evening. Everybody has had it.

loreStory.t: There is a hard edge under the game and the old hands put it there deliberately. Two teeth in every bag are dog. One is off a
Rotjaw
, which will stand at the head of a farm track for a hundred years and never come at you. The other is off a
Blightcur

, which will lie down twenty paces off and not come at you either. A cracker who cannot tell those two apart on a cloth, in good light, with all the time in the world, will one day sit down and rest in the wrong company.

items.name: Spine Bones
items.description: Three vertebrae still loosely strung together. Gravecharger sheds them and does not slow down.
items.loreDesc: Three vertebrae still loosely strung together. Gravecharger sheds them and does not slow down.

loreStory.t: Boil the gristle off, run a cord through the holes, and a spine becomes the cheapest counter anybody ever made: one bone pushed down the string for each night kept.
Jehanne

has used the same one since she took up the rite — a short string, nine bones, because nine was the length of the rota she was handed and it has never been revised down for her. She pushes one along after the candles are out. When the ninth goes she runs them all back to the top and starts again, and she has done that more times than she has a number for, on a rota that has not had nine keepers on it in a very long time. Ten gold buys you the string. What you count on it afterwards is your own business.

items.name: Matted Pelt
items.description: Coarse black fur clumped and matted, with stray quills caught in it. Something out there is patchy now.
items.loreDesc: Coarse black fur clumped and matted, with stray quills caught in it. Something out there is patchy now.

loreStory.t: Nineteen gold. It was nineteen ten years ago and it is nineteen today, and
gold

is supposed to be the only thing in this country that holds a number like that. You cannot card the fur or tan it, and the quills caught through it come off something small that had no business bedding down that close to something that size — which is also why it cannot be faked. A dealer out west set out to break the price and brought forty in at once. He was paid nineteen gold, forty times over, by a factor who counted them out, asked nothing and wrote no name in the book. He has not tried it again, and he has stopped joking about who is at the far end of that chain.

items.name: Mint Slime
items.description: Mint-green, translucent, and lit by a pale core. Every pond blob in the valley leaves one behind, wobbling.
items.loreDesc: Mint-green, translucent, and lit by a pale core. Every pond blob in the valley leaves one behind, wobbling.

loreStory.t: A broken
pond-dweller

leaves the light behind in it, and that light is no use at all for seeing by and perfect for being seen. Set one on a stone at dusk and it is still findable at midnight and gone by the next night, so the valley walkers buy them ten at a time and mark their way in at the junctions.

loreStory: One at a junction means a walker went that way. Two means come and get me. That is the entire code and it has not changed in the working memory of anyone using it. There is a man on the pond circuit who has marked his route in and out for eleven years and has never once set the second, and the fire he walks back to keeps a standing agreement about the night he does: the pot comes off, and everybody goes.

items.name: Mire Claw
items.description: A green-grey claw with fen mud dried in the cracks. Mireglare keeps four sets and uses them all.
items.loreDesc: A green-grey claw with fen mud dried in the cracks. Mireglare keeps four sets and uses them all.

loreStory.t: Never buy a clean one. Fen mud sets into the cracks like grout and it is half the goods: it tells you which bank, which season, and whether the claw has been out of the water as long as the seller says it has. People working
Mireglare

country grade the mud before they so much as look at the point — which is exactly why the fen road has a small trade in mud. There is a man on it who sells the stuff by the thumbful, correct colour, correct bank, and everybody knows, and the grading goes on regardless, because the alternative is saying out loud that the only thing anyone can truly check about a piece of junk is what colour it is.

items.name: Moss Slime
items.description: A green dome flecked with moss, still cool. The forest blobs leave one behind every time they lose.
items.loreDesc: A green dome flecked with moss, still cool. The forest blobs leave one behind every time they lose.

loreStory.t: Cool for hours, and it will not take heat off a hand, which is the only property in this whole part of the trade that a person can actually use.
Jehanne

keeps a crock of them by her fire and puts one on a burn, a barked knuckle, a blister off a bad boot, the way somebody's grandmother did it. Whether any of that is needed here is a question she has stopped raising, on the same reasoning as everything else she still does: the hand hurts, the hand goes cool, the person sits down and stays a while. Seven gold the crock. The wood restocks it every time it loses.

items.name: Driftwood
items.description: Grey, water-worn branches still furred with moss. Cut a Stumpling down and this is most of what is left.
items.loreDesc: Grey, water-worn branches still furred with moss. Break a Stumpling and this is most of what is left.

loreStory.t: The dealers sort by the ends. Water breaks a branch ragged; a blade does not. A bundle with clean ends came off a
Stumpling

that was walking that morning, and it is the same wood, and it burns the same, and it goes for less anyway — six gold, against eight for the honest sort, and it is the cheapest heat there is either way.

loreStory: One shore fire took a load of the cut sort in a wet season and it burned green for the better part of an hour. Nobody said anything about it. The talk went thin and then stopped, and people found reasons to turn in early, and in the morning the fire was banked and swept and somebody had been out to the woodpile in the dark and sorted the whole of it into two heaps.

items.name: Watcher Mask
items.description: Grim steel with cheek guards and a third eye graven above the slits. The fiends that wore it had spares.
items.loreDesc: Grim steel with cheek guards and a third eye cut above the slits. Somebody hammered it, and that is the comfort.

loreStory.t: A bag coming back off the ground where
Grinmask

works can have two masks in it, and telling them apart takes no expertise at all. This one is hammer work. The inside is a mess of tool marks, the strap boss has been replaced by a hand that could not match the original rivet, and the third eye above the brow was cut freehand and sits a hair off the centre line, by a man who noticed, and shrugged, and sold it anyway. It is grim on purpose. Grim was what the customer wanted.

loreStory: The other kind has no marks in it anywhere, and the trade does not price that kind, and does not carry it at the top of the bag.

Ninety-five gold, and there are crackers who wear this one working the same ground it came off. Ask them why and they will tell you about the cheek guards. The cheek guards are a quarter-inch of soft steel and would not stop a dog.

items.name: Opal Shell
items.description: A curved flake of shell that runs green to gold as you turn it. The dune keeps giving these up.
items.loreDesc: A curved flake of shell that runs green to gold as you turn it. The dune keeps giving these up.
loreStory: Somebody on the dune circuit worked out that a flake on a wire turns in the wind, and a turning flake throws green, then gold, then nothing, over and over, further into the dark than firelight carries. So the dune fires wear collars of them now: two dozen strung along a wire between the stones, flashing all night, so that a person out there with no idea where they are has something to walk at.

loreStory.t: The wire outlasts the keeper.
Gunnar

has come in on four of them and found cold stones and no one, and he has left every wire hanging. His reasoning is short and he does not offer it twice: the flashing still fetches a stranger to a windbreak, a ring of stones and somewhere out of the sand, and that is not nothing, and it is a great deal more than the dark straight on.

items.name: Beast Molars
items.description: Two grinders with forked roots, one big enough for a Diretusk. Both chewed harder things than grass.
items.loreDesc: Two grinders with forked roots, one big enough for a Diretusk. Both chewed harder things than grass.

loreStory.t: Nine gold, and worth it only to the one man on that road who can read them. Hand him a molar and he will give you the animal and the age to the season: a
Nightmule
's at eleven years, a
Diretusk

's at more than he has numbers for, a brute's not at all, because a brute grinds against rock and its teeth lie about the years. He was a horseman. He is not a great deal else now. People bring him teeth for the trick and he does the trick, and they pay him in company, which is the going rate. What he cannot do is name the last horse he owned. He has been asked twice, kindly, by two different people, each of whom decided afterwards not to ask again.

items.name: Shadow Claw
items.description: A matched pair of glossy black hooks, sharp as the day they grew. Duskfang and its cousins do not give them up.
items.loreDesc: A matched pair of glossy black hooks, sharp as the day they grew. Duskfang and its cousins do not give them up.

loreStory.t: Worn on a thong, a matched pair says one thing and says it loudly: I have stood in front of a
Duskfang
and I am here to be asked about it.

loreStory: A woman on the black-wood rounds wore hers for two years before she had earned them. She bought them, eight over the going rate, from a man who knew precisely what she was buying and handed them across without a word about it. She has since done the thing twice, properly, with people watching, which by any reckoning settles the account. She still will not take them off. The man is still on that road and still nods to her at the crossing, and in all the years since neither of them has said one syllable about it, and she has worked out by now that the nod is the part she cannot give up.

items.name: Bone Beetle
items.description: Palm-sized and bone-pale, its plated back mottled tan, six legs tucked under. The valley's small fry all carry one.
items.loreDesc: Palm-sized and bone-pale, its plated back mottled tan, six legs tucked under. The valley's small fry all carry one.

loreStory.t: Twelve gold is a lot for a common thing, and the reason is that they are a nuisance to reach: they sit deep, and you have to break a
Sprigling

open properly to get one out. Children manage it faster than grown men and for less. So a pale beetle in a child's pocket is a confession — it says which end of the valley, on which afternoon, against what they were told. Most of that road has agreed not to notice. Twelve gold is twelve gold, and the sacks pay for boots.

items.name: Pale Wing
items.description: Tan membrane on pale finger bones, torn free mid-flight. The gaunt things that haunt the drifts fly on these.
items.loreDesc: Tan membrane on pale finger bones, torn free mid-flight. The gaunt things that haunt the drifts fly on these.

loreStory.t: Eleven hundred and six. A woman on the north road has walked the same two miles of drift at every thaw for thirty years, picking pale wings out of the melt, and that is her count. They come down whole and they come down alone — no other bone, no fur, no teeth, nothing else of whatever was carrying them, not once in eleven hundred. She sells enough to keep herself in boots and no more. Every autumn she sends the year's figure to
the Chronicle
with no letter attached, because there is nothing to say about it yet. What she wants is to be there in the year the number stops.

items.name: Frost Quartz
items.description: Ice-blue spires on a common base, cold indoors and out. Rimeshard grows this in its rock and swings the rest.
items.loreDesc: Ice-blue spires on a common base, cold indoors and out. Rimeshard grows this in its rock and swings the rest.
loreStory: The test is your own neck. Hold a spire under the jaw for a slow count of twenty. True frost quartz does not come up to meet you — it stays precisely as cold as it was, and afterwards the skin aches. Dyed quartz warms by about eight. An honest seller offers you the count before you ask for it.

loreStory.t: The forgers got around this in the obvious way. They sell in hard weather, when everything in the world is cold and the count proves nothing, and they sell to people three weeks out of
the grass
, who do not yet know that anything here is bought or sold, and who will hand over a coin they carried through an entire life for a stone that is going to disappoint them in April.

items.name: Rime Stones
items.description: Blue-white pebbles, a good dozen, that will not melt in the palm. Whatever a Frostling is packed from, this is it.
items.loreDesc: Blue-white pebbles, a good dozen, that will not melt in the palm. Whatever a Frostling is packed from, this is it.
loreStory: They are sold by the dozen because the game takes twelve. Every era that arrives here brought its own version — knucklebones, jacks, five-stones — and rime pebbles are what the game settled on in the cold country, being the one counter that will not warm, wear, or roll off true.

loreStory.t: There is a patch on the north side of the meadow with eleven of them still in the grass, in a rough ring, where a throw was interrupted a long time ago.
Solveig
cuts around it. Asked why she does not just gather them up, she says she will. The twelfth is in her apron pocket and has been for nine years.

items.name: Curved Horn
items.description: A pale horn with a clean spiral, snapped at the base. Gravecharger wears a pair and notices neither.
items.loreDesc: A pale horn with one clean curve, snapped at the base. Gravecharger wears a pair and notices neither.
loreStory: Split it, boil it soft, press it flat and it goes translucent: four panes to a horn, thin enough to see a flame through and tough enough to laugh at wind. That is the horner's whole trade, and the reason a fire on an open fell stays lit in weather. A pane costs less than a candle and outlives forty of them.

loreStory.t: The joke among horners is that the finest stock in the country grows on
Gravecharger

, and getting any is a matter of standing in the right place at a very wrong moment. In fact they walk its lines, which run straight and are close to the last straight thing out that way, and pick up what it sheds and does not miss. Every lantern on the old eastern circuit was glazed like this, back when there was a circuit. The horners are still cutting panes, and could not tell you now who buys them.

items.name: Grey Matter
items.description: Whole, pink and unpleasantly warm. Palehusk carries spares, which explains a great deal about Palehusk.
items.loreDesc: Whole, pink and unpleasantly warm. Palehusk carries spares, which explains a great deal about Palehusk.

loreStory.t: Thirty-five gold is most of a week, and it comes out of the head, and the head is the last thing you do. There is a woman on the black-rock circuit who brings in four or five a season and is entirely plain about it: feet first, work upward, bag open on the stone and not in your lap. She says releasing at the counter and
the other word

at the fire, and means both. Warm is not the same as occupied, she says. Holding that difference is the whole of the job, and anybody who cannot hold it should go and do something else, with her blessing, today.
She keeps one rule that has nothing to do with the work. When it is
one of the person-shaped ones
, she closes the hand first — folds the open fingers over, before she starts on anything else. It does nothing for the shape. It is not for the shape.

items.name: Pale Eye
items.description: A grey eye with the light gone out of it. Palehusk collects them, which is not a comforting thought.
items.loreDesc: A grey eye with the light gone out of it. Palehusk collects them, which is not a comforting thought.

loreStory.t: A sorter at the fen counter set one aside out of a new bag and asked the plain question: where on the animal was it. The cracker could not say. Neither could the next one asked, nor anyone on that road since. They are picked out of the grass afterwards, at the edge of the pressed circle, loose, never attached to the thing that came down. And what
that one
leaves is a mask, and the mask has no eyes in it and never had; the inward side is smooth.

loreStory: So the trade did what the trade does. Named it Pale Eye, priced it at twenty-six, agreed the price, stopped asking. Ask at a stall today and you will be told they come off Grinmask, which is where they come from and not where they were.

items.name: Pale Claw
items.description: A cream claw hooked like a reaping tool, ragged at the socket. Bergclaw grows ten and uses all of them.
items.loreDesc: A cream claw hooked like a reaping tool, ragged at the socket. Bergclaw grows ten and uses all of them.

loreStory.t: North-rounds buyers price these by where they were picked up, which is not how anything else in the trade is priced. Off open ground, twenty-four gold. Found inside a fire's ring of stones, whatever the buyer can be talked into — and there is no agreed figure, because there has never yet been an instance. That is
Bergclaw

in one price: it comes for the warmth, sits out past the edge of the light the whole night, and leaves a claw in the sand for whoever slept badly. Keepers do not sell those. They carry them about in a pocket for a season or two, and that pocket is how the trade knows which fires had a visitor last winter.

items.name: Moth Wing
items.description: Pale tan and ribbed brown, with a blue sheen at the base. Something big and soft-winged shed it in the dark.
items.loreDesc: Pale tan and ribbed brown, with a blue sheen at the base. Something big and soft-winged shed it in the dark.

loreStory.t: Handle one and a little of it comes away on your thumb, and what comes away does not go back. Most of the trade runs on that: an honest seller keeps them in paper, and the paper is the first thing to check, because a clean sheet means it has been touched twice and a floured one means it has been touched a hundred times. The bare ones are not fakes. They are the ones somebody carried in a pocket for a long while and finally sold.
Hearn
's is bare, and he did not sell it.

items.name: Ivory Horns
items.description: Four ivory horns splayed from one base, ridged like bark. Fiends and wraiths grow them for arguments they win.
items.loreDesc: Four ivory horns splayed from one base, ridged like bark. Fiends and wraiths grow them for arguments they win.
loreStory: Twenty-four gold, and the honest bone in it is worth about two. What you are buying is the outline — four horns off one base, ridged like bark, and no other arrangement of plain bone in this country reads as hard as that across a room. The traders know precisely what they have. It goes high on the stack, three-quarters on, with the light coming up under it.

loreStory.t: It is the newly woken who buy them. A man three weeks into a country that is not the one he expected will not spend on a blanket and will spend on this, and hang it on a wall he does not own, in a room he will not keep, and it works — it is the first thing here that is his.
Solveig
has watched that happen a hundred times from the fire, and has never once talked anybody out of it.

items.name: Silk Skein
items.description: Silvery cord wound tight and bound at the waist, cool to the touch. No hand in Nangijala spun this one.
items.loreDesc: Silvery cord wound tight and bound at the waist, cool to the touch. No hand in Nangijala spun this one.

loreStory.t: They arrive. Four or five a season at
Jehanne

's door, always overnight, always wound the same way and bound at the waist with the same two-turn knot, and in nine years she has not once caught whoever leaves them. No hand spun the cord — look close and the strands are laid rather than twisted — but a hand wound it into a skein and a hand tied that knot, and a knot is a habit, and a habit is a person. It is the strongest thread anybody here has, and twenty-six gold is cheap for it. Jehanne does not sell hers. She puts bread out on the nights she thinks one is coming, and the bread goes, and she has stopped telling people about it — the last time she did, three of them offered to sit up and watch with her, and she said no rather too fast.

items.name: Hornet Nest
items.description: Tan paper in banded layers, one dark doorway low on the side. Prised out of a Stumpling's moss, and empty. Mostly.
items.loreDesc: Tan paper in banded layers, one dark doorway low on the side. Prised out of a Stumpling's moss, and empty. Mostly.

loreStory.t: Boiled down it makes a passable paper, grey and tough, and that is the whole reason a nest is worth twenty-six gold while a handful of moss is worth nothing. The bands are worth more than the paper to the right buyer: one band a season, so a nest the size of a head has been building for eleven years, and the
Stumpling
carrying it has been standing in one spot that long. Put a stick in the doorway before it goes in your bag. Then wait. The man who taught everyone that rule is the man who did not.

items.name: Rose Quartz
items.description: A spray of pink spires on a rough base. Pretty enough that people forget what they had to kill for it.
items.loreDesc: A spray of pink spires on a rough base. Pretty enough that people forget it came out of something that was walking.

loreStory.t: It takes no edge, holds no heat and does nothing whatever, which is why the trade calls it the coming-home stone. You have been a month on the road, you smell of
somebody else's leavings
, and you cannot make what you have been doing sound like a job — so you bring back the one thing in the bag that is only pretty.

loreStory: There is a woman on the west road with thirty-one of them along a windowsill and a husband still adding to them. She counted once, and worked out that she can name every month he was away and not one thing he did in it. She keeps them out anyway. She has thought it through and decided the sill is not a reproach; it is only the shape a marriage takes when one of you goes out and comes back.

items.name: Pitted Ring
items.description: Thick hammered silver, tarnished and pitted all over, off a Palehusk's borrowed finger. It fits nobody at all.
items.loreDesc: Thick hammered silver, tarnished and pitted all over. It was measured for a finger, and not the one it came off.
loreStory: A ring is the one thing in the trade that arrives with a measurement already on it. A jeweller sat down with a hand in front of him and cut this to fit it. Everything else off a broken shape has to be guessed at, but a band goes on a rod and reads off as a number, and the number was a person.

loreStory.t: So the crackers going through what a
Palehusk
leaves take the size before they take the price. It costs nothing and it takes a moment, and
Bettany

pays for the figures whether or not she wants the ring. She has four pages of them now. Size, date, where. Not one name against any of them and no way left of getting one, and she keeps the pages in order anyway, because a measurement is a detail, and details are the first thing to go.

loreStory: Eighteen gold. It is a small ring, and it did not fit.

items.name: Beast Eye
items.description: Whole and damp, a brown iris in a veined tan ball. The fiends that carry spares will not miss this one.
items.loreDesc: Whole and damp, a brown iris in a veined tan ball. The fiends that carry spares will not miss this one.
loreStory: Whole or worth nothing. That is the first hard lesson of the trade and it gets learned on these, because they are the commonest eye out there and sixteen gold is real money to someone on a first bag. A burst one is a wet mark on a cloth. So you learn the spoon — the shape of it, the angle, exactly how much you can hurry and where you cannot — and you learn it at night, at the edge of a fire, from somebody who has already finished their own bag and could be asleep.

loreStory.t: Everyone in the trade can tell you who taught them the spoon. Not the first buyer who paid them properly, not the crossing where they lost a boot: the person who sat back down in the cold with someone else's leavings and showed them how.
Both of the trade's words
get used about this work, and neither of them covers that.

items.name: Prism Quill
items.description: One long quill that shifts through every colour as it turns. No bird anyone has flushed grows these.
items.loreDesc: One long quill that shifts through every colour as it turns. No bird anyone has flushed grows these.

loreStory.t: Sixty gold buys a great many fakes. The usual method is a common quill, four dyes and a patient afternoon, and it is good enough at a lamplit stall to have taken most people at least once. The test costs nothing: turn it slowly. A dyed feather goes through its colours one at a time. A true one holds two at once, and the seam between them slides. The woman who taught
the trade
that test made the fakes for eleven years, says so freely, and is paid now to stand at the far end of the table looking bored.

items.name: Iris Petals
items.description: Purple petals with pale wedged stems, gathered past bloom. Meadow blobs trail them wherever they bounce.
items.loreDesc: Purple petals with pale wedged stems, gathered past bloom. Meadow blobs trail them wherever they bounce.

loreStory.t: Hold one up against an
Emberwing

's wing at ten paces — closer is a mistake, and the tellers have the name of the man who tried it — and the banding matches. Violet, then the pink line, then violet again, then the pale wedge at the base where the petal leaves the stem. Not similar. The same, down to where the colour changes.

loreStory: Which means the wing was copied. Which means that on the other side of all this, on an afternoon nobody wrote down, a person lay on their front in a meadow with their face a hand's width from an iris and looked long enough and hard enough to keep it. They were not thinking about being remembered. They were looking at a flower. Twenty-two gold off any stall on the road, and the closest thing to a picture of one living hour that anyone here will ever hold.

items.name: Venom Claw
items.description: Pulled from an Ashfiend before it crumbled. The purple hook is fine, but the green crust on the tip is not.
items.loreDesc: A purple hook with one pale ridge of light down the curve, and a hard green crust dried on the last third of the point.

loreStory.t: It grew where it sits — the one thing off an
Ashfiend

that did. Longer than a finger, curved well past use, the base a socket shaped around a knuckle that is not there any more. Hafted, it makes a poor knife every time, and people keep the poor knife, because a claw is worth little and a claw with a hand behind it is worth something.

loreStory: The crust on the point is the part worth money: mustard at its base, hard green at the tip, sitting on the purple rather than in it. It was put there; it did not grow there. It flakes under a thumbnail, so the careful carry one point-down in a stiff wrap and wash afterwards.

loreStory.t: Bettany
pays over the odds for a well-crusted one, and she is not buying knives. The same green comes off
the pale walking thing
on the black rock, and two creatures' leavings agreeing about a pigment is the kind of sentence
the Chronicle

exists to catch. Whether this point put the green into something or drew it out, the crust will not say. She keeps her best one wrapped in linen inside a chapter that has no words in it yet — just the claw, and a heading: which way did it run.

items.name: Void Flesh
items.description: A lump of violet meat that keeps twitching toward your hand. Voidmaw is mostly this, on the inside.
items.loreDesc: A lump of violet meat that keeps twitching toward your hand. Voidmaw is mostly this, on the inside.

loreStory.t: No use has ever been found for it. It will not cure, will not render, will not take a dye, and it twitches toward warmth for two days and then lies still. It also carries a standing price — fifty-five,
in gold
, the same at every stall on the road — which no scrap in this trade has any business carrying. A standing price is not a fact about a lump of meat. It is a fact about somebody who wants one.

loreStory: A cracker off the fen followed the collection cart once, to see. Two days out, and on the second night the road he had come up was not where he had left it, so he walked home the long way. He has not sold any since; he leaves his on the stone where he finds it. He will give you his reasons at some length, and not one of them is the reason.

items.name: Prism Plume
items.description: Banded blue through green to red down a tan quill. Whatever grew a tail of these has not shown itself yet.
items.loreDesc: Banded blue through green to red down a tan quill. Whatever grew a tail of these has not shown itself yet.

loreStory.t: Gunnar

measured one: quill at the base as thick as a bowstring, vane a hand and a half, and a tail wants a dozen at least before it is a tail. From that he got a span. From the span, a weight. From the weight, what a thing that size has to eat in a week and how much country that takes to find it in. He wrote the number down and he has not said it to anyone. What he will say, pushed, is that the country in question would have to be country people walk through, and that people walk through it.

items.name: Raw Meat
items.description: Thick, red, rimmed with brown fat. Which beast it came off is between you, the cook, and nobody else.
items.loreDesc: Thick, red, rimmed with brown fat. Which beast it came off is between you, the cook, and nobody else.
loreStory: Hunger here is a habit rather than a need, which makes ten gold of meat the strangest purchase in the trade: you are not buying food, you are buying three hours. A slab that size wants turning, and a spit wants somebody sat at it, and people who would never sit down for a telling will sit down for a plate.

loreStory.t: Solveig
buys the biggest she can afford rather than the best, for exactly that reason.
The newly woken

come up off the grass unable to give their own names and most of them want to walk off into the dark and be elsewhere; a person holding a plate stays where they are for as long as it takes to eat it, which is generally long enough for someone to ask them one true thing. The cooking is the courtesy. The meat is only how it gets paid for.

items.name: Blood Gills
items.description: A fan of red frills that keeps twitching after it is cut. Voidmaw breathes through a hundred of them.
items.loreDesc: A fan of red frills that keeps twitching after it is cut. Voidmaw breathes through a hundred of them.

loreStory.t: The twitch runs out along the fan and back again, and it slows on a schedule steady enough to sell. Fresh, about twice a breath. By evening, once in ten. Nothing by morning. Which makes a fan off
the ringed mouth

lying in a road a clock: something was broken here, and you can say within the hour how long ago, and from that how far ahead of you the party is and roughly what kind of day they are having. Fen-walkers read one off the ground without breaking stride. It works about as well as anything out there works, and it is the only good reason anyone has to be glad of the twitching, which is otherwise the least popular thing in the bag.

items.name: Red Scale
items.description: A palm of deep red scales, each one overlapping the next. Emberjaw sheds them where it basks.
items.loreDesc: A palm of deep red scales, each one overlapping the next. Emberjaw sheds them where it basks.

loreStory.t: Everybody who works the black rock walks on
Emberjaw

. That stone cooks a boot sole in a day and a half; a palm of red scale, cut to shape and stitched on with the overlap running heel to toe, does a season. Thirty gold, never argued, because the alternative is coming back barefoot over ground that stays warm the whole way.

loreStory: The cobblers read the returned soles the way other people read a road. Even wear, heel to toe: he walked in and he walked out. Worn through at the toe on both feet and nowhere else: he ran, a long way, and did not turn round to see what he was running from. There is a cobbler at the last fire who keeps the bad ones in a box under his bench. He will show you if you ask twice, and he will not give you the names, because half of them still come in for resoling.

items.name: Cloth Roll
items.description: Coarse grey canvas off a Nightmule's pack, rolled tight and trailing a tail. Tents do not sew themselves.
items.loreDesc: Coarse grey canvas off a Nightmule's pack, rolled tight and trailing a tail. Tents do not sew themselves.

loreStory.t: Open it out and it is a tent for one. Cut close, no room in it for a second set of shoulders. The original seams are double-sewn and even, the work of somebody taught properly, with time to do it right. Then, later, in different thread and in a hurry: four more tie-points added down one edge, punched through and whipped round by a hand that had plainly never done it before, so that a flap could be pegged out to the side. Somebody turned a one-man tent into a shelter for two, badly, on the road. The badly-made ties are the ones still holding. That is the whole of what is known about them — that there were two, that one of them could not sew, and that the canvas came down off
an animal that is carrying nothing at all now
and has not been pitched in a very long time.

items.name: Rotten Hide
items.description: Grey hide gone soft, with stitching still holding two ends that never matched. It smells exactly as it looks.
items.loreDesc: Grey hide gone soft, with stitching still holding two ends that never matched. It smells exactly as it looks.

loreStory.t: It is not a hide. A saddler at the fires took one look at the seam and said so, flatly, in front of the man selling it: that is a repair. Two skins that never matched, joined with a whip-stitch worked from the inside so the mend would not show — trouble nobody takes except on a garment somebody expected to be seen in. Small stitches, a poor needle, a great deal of patience. It came off one of
the walking things on the black rock

, which is where such things end up, and the crackers price it at nine gold on account of the smell. The saddler handed his back and would not take the coin for it. He made no speech about it. He simply did not want the money, and the man who brought it in has kept it since, unsold, in a sack behind the door.

items.name: Rough Stone
items.description: Cracked brown rock with flat faceted sides. Half the things that shed it were walking around a moment ago.
items.loreDesc: Cracked brown rock with flat faceted sides. Half the things that shed it were walking around a moment ago.

loreStory.t: Learn to read the flats and this stops being a rock worth four. Weather leaves a face rounded and evenly pitted. A hammer leaves a bruise with a centre to it. Teeth leave parallel scoring, wide-set, the same gauge every time, with a shallow dish where the tusk turned — and a stone scored like that is not a rock any more, it is a measurement of
Gnashjaw

's jaw, taken by the jaw. The sorters pay eleven for a clean bite and twelve if the scoring runs off the edge, because that means the animal was working on something larger and did not finish. Nothing else on the bench triples in price for having been chewed. Everything else on the bench is a piece of a creature. This is a piece of what one did.

items.name: Clawed Foot
items.description: Three cream claws on a brown scaled foot, cut clean at the joint. An Emberjaw's still holds its heat.
items.loreDesc: Three cream claws on a brown scaled foot, cut clean at the joint. An Emberjaw's still holds its heat.

loreStory.t: An
Emberjaw

's foot comes off the black rock warm and stays warm, and every keeper on the cold rounds has wanted one at four in the morning. What the sellers leave out — because it is bad for business, and because it takes years to notice — is that the warmth is not a property of the foot. It is a property of how often the foot gets talked about.

loreStory: A keeper on the north circuit held hers hot for nine winters by telling the same story over it most nights, to whoever was sitting there: where she got it, what the animal was doing, what the rock smelled like underneath. Then she got tired of the story. She says she can close her hand round it now and feel nothing at all, and she tells people that instead, which works, and which she finds a good deal funnier than they do.

items.name: Small Teeth
items.description: A scatter of little teeth, none of them matching. Small things lose them; smaller things collect them.
items.loreDesc: A scatter of little teeth, none of them matching. Small things lose them; smaller things collect them.
loreStory: Six gold the scatter, which does not cover the stooping, and every bag in the trade has some in the bottom seam regardless. You pick them up without deciding to. Then the bag goes on the counter, out they come with the sweepings, and the trader takes them by weight at a price he did not set and tips them into a barrel with everything else too small to have a name.

loreStory.t: Ask who buys a barrel of teeth and he will tell you the truth, which is that he has no idea. The order comes down the road, the barrel goes up it, the gold comes back, and it has worked that way longer than he has been standing there.
Bettany
has followed that road three times and come back with three answers, each of them a further stretch of road.

items.name: Carapace
items.description: A plate of segmented shell, scuffed from digging. Dunedelver sheds them the way a road sheds gravel.
items.loreDesc: A plate of segmented shell, scuffed from digging. Dunedelver sheds them the way a road sheds gravel.

loreStory.t: There are still legs on it. Six or eight little dry stubs around the rim, snapped short, because a
Dunedelver

comes out of this the way a man comes out of a coat and walks off out of the leg cases as it goes. That is the whole difference between this and the rest of a bag: nothing had to be broken for it. The animal is out there right now, one size bigger, and its old back is in your hand.

loreStory: The trade finds that unsettling and cannot defend the feeling. A bag of teeth is a bag of endings and no one flinches at it. A carapace is a thing somebody outgrew, lying in the sand looking exactly like a leaving without being one, and there are buyers who will handle them all day and buyers who will not have them in with the rest.

items.name: Scaled Paw
items.description: Mottled grey-green hide and three pale curled claws. A Palemaw leaves them, and never in matching pairs.
items.loreDesc: Mottled grey-green hide and three pale curled claws. A Palemaw leaves them, and never in matching pairs.
loreStory: This is what a new cracker learns on. The hide is almost exactly the thickness of everything they will ever have to open, the joint sits where joints sit, and at thirty gold you can ruin a dozen learning where the blade goes. Three passes. You have done it right when the claws come away still hooked to one another.

loreStory.t: Sigrun

keeps a crate by the forge door and charges nothing for what comes out of it. She will not stand over anybody while they cut, either. What she does is ask one question, some days after their first real one, and it is not how it went and it is not what it fetched: she asks which of the two words they used about it afterwards. Everyone she has asked remembers being asked, years on, and not one of them can say precisely why it stayed.

items.name: Horn Spur
items.description: A stub of horn broken off at the base. Gnashjaw grinds its tusks down and this is what falls off.
items.loreDesc: A stub of horn broken off at the base. Gnashjaw grinds its tusks down and this is what falls off.

loreStory.t: Six gold buys a thumb of horn with a hook on the end — what comes off a
Gnashjaw

working its tusks down on a boulder — and for one season every coat at three fires on that road was fastened at the throat with one, because a man at the middle fire wore his that way and people copy.

loreStory: He did not start it on purpose. He had woken with nothing, the way everyone does, picked the spur off the path on his first walk out, and put it on the coat because a coat wants fastening. By the time the third fire had taken up the fashion he could no longer have told you the path or the season, and he had begun saying it had been his wife's, which it had not, and the people who knew that let him have it.

items.name: Milk Tooth
items.description: A tooth the size of a fingernail, root and all. Something small lost it, and something small missed it.
items.loreDesc: A tooth the size of a fingernail, root and all. Something small lost it, and something small missed it.

loreStory.t: Four gold, which is the least the trade pays for anything, and there is one at nearly every fire, kept in a knot of cloth by somebody who cannot tell you what it came off. There was a man on
Wendell

's stretch of the east road who asked everyone he met the same question: do hedgehogs have milk teeth. He would produce the tooth, hold it out flat on his palm, and wait. He had had it a great deal longer than he had had the reason for it. People said yes, mostly — a
Quillkin
sheds them and they are all over the low country — and he would put it away satisfied and ask again the next season, because the asking was the part he could still lose.

items.name: Black Egg
items.description: A smooth black egg, warm on one side. Nobody knows what is in it, and nobody is volunteering to wait.
items.loreDesc: A smooth black egg, warm on one face and cold on the other. Every year somebody pays soulstone money for one.

loreStory.t: Two tests, and a new cracker has both inside a week. Put the find to the inside of the wrist and count ten:
a hard piece

is warm the whole way round, and this is warm on one face only, the other going cold against you as you count. Then set a knife-point to it. A hard piece takes no mark; this takes a grey line. Junk, then — twenty-eight gold, and worth it, because they polish, and a black one on a shelf looks like money.

loreStory: Which is the whole trouble. The man who works them at the ford sells to people three days woken who have heard the word and never held one, and he has never once said it. He says egg. Clearly, every time, and then waits, and lets the buyer supply the rest. He is quite right that he has not lied. The trade has a word for him anyway.

items.name: River Stone
items.description: Worn smooth, grey-blue and cold in the palm. Every pond blob keeps one, and none of them will say why.
items.loreDesc: Worn smooth, grey-blue and cold in the palm. Every pond blob keeps one, and none of them will say why.
loreStory: Four. The cheapest thing sold in Nangijala, and nearly the only one where the buyer volunteers what it is for: a hand at a fire wants a job while the mouth does the hard part, and a smooth stone is a job. The tellers keep a bowl of them by the log. At most fires you are not asked your name until you have picked one up.

loreStory.t: As for the
Puddlings
