— a woman who spent a season at the shallows watching them says she has the answer and it is not interesting, only sad. A thing made of water needs one part of itself that stays put. Otherwise it has no way of knowing which direction is down.

items.name: Soft Plume
items.description: A long plume shading violet to gold, impossibly soft. Nothing in the roster has feathers like this.
items.loreDesc: A long plume shading violet to gold, softer than anything else on the stall, and off nothing anyone has seen.

loreStory.t: It is useless. Too soft to write with, too soft to fletch, too limp to trim a hat that would hold its shape in any wind. It has one use and it is on no list. You put it into the hand of somebody who has just woken and cannot stop shaking, because a hand holding something shakes less, and because it is the first pleasant thing this country has given them.
Jehanne
carries three, buys more than she needs, and does not call it a rite.

items.name: Snow Tuft
items.description: A burr of white fur bristling every way, blue in its shadows. Warm to wear, and slow to finish thawing.
items.loreDesc: A burr of white fur bristling every way, blue in its shadows. Warm to wear, and slow to finish thawing.

loreStory.t: It comes off thorn scrub and fence wire on the passes, wherever the white things have gone through —
Winterfang

leaves it by the handful and never comes back for it. The seller at the north market has one rule and will not sell to anyone who breaks it: take a tuft bare-handed and hold it until it stops being cold. That is about a minute. The cold comes out of it into you first, all of it, before any warmth arrives, and a man who sews a hood full of it without knowing that gets an hour on the road worse than no hood at all — which is precisely the hour a cold man decides to sit down and rest a moment. Twenty gold. Half the young crackers think the minute is theatre. He lets them think so, and he still will not sell to one who lets go early.

items.name: Split Bones
items.description: Cracked long bones, split for marrow by something with no patience. Rotjaw leaves piles of them.
items.loreDesc: Cracked long bones, split for marrow by something with no patience. Rotjaw leaves piles of them.

loreStory.t: A jaw splits a long bone the long way, following the grain, and leaves the halves rocking where they fell. A person splits one across, with a rock, because a person wants the marrow out and does not much care about the bone afterwards. Every guide teaches the difference in the first hour, and
Hearn
teaches it as an order: look at the split before you look at anything else.

loreStory: He has his reasons. A cracker new to that country came over a rise, found cracked bone scattered round a hollow, decided he was standing in somebody's camp, and sat down in it to wait for company. What came was not company. He re-formed beside a fire two nights later, short the whole afternoon and most of his reasons for being out there at all, and he tells it himself now, badly, to anyone who will sit.

items.name: Gloom Cap
items.description: Fat violet cap, pale freckles, thick lavender stem. It grows on Stumplings, which should tell you plenty.
items.loreDesc: Fat violet cap, pale freckles, thick lavender stem. It grows on Stumplings, which should tell you plenty.

loreStory.t: A
Stumpling

will stand and let you work. You can take four caps off the shoulder of one, unhurried, with it watching you do it, and it will not shift its weight the whole time — and then the basket is full, and the job is done, and the entire problem is in front of you, which is getting back out of the clearing.

loreStory: So watch a picker leave a wood sometime. They go backwards. Slowly, basket held to the chest, feeling behind for roots with one heel, all the way to the tree line, eyes front the whole distance. Nothing about it is dignified. Everyone who has tried it facing the other way agrees the silliness is worth twenty-four gold a cap, and they do not go into detail, and they change the subject well.

items.name: Silver Bars
items.description: Three cast bars, stamped and stacked. Somebody smelted these, and somebody else never delivered them.
items.loreDesc: Three cast bars, stamped and stacked. Somebody smelted these, and somebody else never delivered them.

loreStory.t: Halvard
will weigh them, quote you low, and not move. He does not doubt the metal. It is that
gold

is the one substance everybody out of every century remembers identically, and silver is not on that list. Silver arrives arguing. His buyers came out of lives a thousand years apart and every one of them knows exactly what silver is worth, and no two of the numbers agree, and a pedlar who prices in coin and keeps walking can afford one argument a day at the outside.

loreStory: So a hundred and eighty gold in bars is a fortune that has to be re-agreed at every counter on the road, which is what makes the stamp worth reading. It is a house mark, not a man's name, and the house is not anywhere now. Somebody at the far end waited on a delivery that never came, and it is worth being exact about why: the bars were not lost. They are right here, three of them, stacked as they were poured. It was the road that went.

items.name: Marrow Bone
items.description: Knobbed at both ends and stained where beige should not be. A Palemaw was busy with it before you were.
items.loreDesc: Knobbed at both ends and stained where beige should not be. A Palemaw was busy with it before you were.
loreStory: Six gold. The cheapest thing on the counter and the most bought, and it does not go into anybody's work — it goes in a pot.

Every fire has one on the boil most evenings. Marrow, an onion if the ground has been generous, whatever the day turned up, and it sits at the edge of the coals doing nothing urgent while the talk goes on over the top of it. Nobody at a fire has ever gone hungry, and it has never been established whether that is because of the pot.

loreStory.t: The stained ones — knobbed, gouged, brown where beige belongs — come off ground a
Palemaw

is working, and the crackers who bring them in scrub them and sell them and say nothing, because a bone out of that mouth boils like any other, and a stall that explains where its stock has been is a stall that stops selling.

items.name: Straw Nest
items.description: A knot of straw pressed into a bowl by something that slept in it. Still warm, occasionally.
items.loreDesc: A knot of straw pressed into a bowl by something that slept in it. Still warm, occasionally.
loreStory: Sold off the same board as the tinder, worth about as much, and there is only the one selling point — which a seller demonstrates by taking your wrist and putting your hand down into the middle of it. Usually it is cold. Now and then it is not, and then you are buying a bed out from under something due back within the hour, and the price goes up rather than down, because people are people.

loreStory.t: Look before you let anyone put your hand in. A
Quillkin

sheds as it sleeps, the quills go in barbed and come out worse, and every dealer on that road can point you at the man who found this out in front of a crowd. He tells it himself now. He holds up the three fingers.

items.name: Rough Hide
items.description: Pegged square with little wooden stakes, edges left ragged. Somebody began the tanning and gave up on it.
items.loreDesc: Pegged square with little wooden stakes, edges left ragged. Somebody began the tanning and gave up on it.

loreStory.t: Tanning is not difficult. It is only long: the same work, at the same hour, in the same place, for weeks — and the last part is what has gone out of this country. To peg a hide out is a promise that you will still be standing over this ground in a month, and the roads move and the fires go out.
Wendell

remembers when a hide pegged in a yard meant nothing at all: that the yard would be there next month was not a thing anyone wondered about. So half-tanned squares come into the trade constantly, and are worth fourteen gold and a shrug. Except that the pegs are still in this one. It was lifted off the ground and rolled up with its stakes, which is not what you do with a job you have given up on. It is what you do with a job you mean to finish somewhere else.

items.name: Down Feather
items.description: One soft tan feather, barbs still perfect. It came off something that flies, which narrows it down little.
items.loreDesc: One soft tan feather, barbs still perfect. It came off something that flies, which narrows it down little.

loreStory.t: Six gold, and it takes something like four hundred to fill a bolster. Three of the four rooms at
the Long Table

are shut, and in one of them a bolster has been getting fatter for years, a handful at a time, by whoever is passing, with nobody organising it. It is not for anyone in particular. It is the bed a person would be put in, if a person came, and it is ready.

items.name: Cobweb
items.description: A torn sheet of web, still sticky at the anchor threads. Nothing in this valley admits to spinning it.
items.loreDesc: A torn sheet of web, still sticky at the anchor threads. Nothing in this valley admits to spinning it.
loreStory: Six gold, the cheapest thing in the trade, and it sells steadily all year. Ask a dealer who buys web and he will tell you: people with doors. A thread pulled across a doorway at shin height, stuck down on the tacky ends, tells you in the morning whether anything came through in the night.

loreStory.t: There is a man at a lapsed fire out on the western grass who strings one every evening. It has never been broken. He is not checking for what comes in: he has been
Faded

two years, he knows the order these things go in, and what he needs to know each morning is whether he went out — whether a shape stood up in the night and walked a round of the yard wearing his hands. He has begun setting a second thread at the back door, having worked out that a man in that condition would use the door he always used, and it was never the front.

items.name: Teal Quill
items.description: Teal at the base, gold at the tip, and light as nothing. Scribes want the bird; nobody has found the bird.
items.loreDesc: Teal at the base, gold at the tip, and light as nothing. Scribes want the bird; nobody has found the bird.

loreStory.t: Split, cut and shaved it makes a better nib than iron: it holds ink through a whole line and it does not weep in wet weather.
Bettany

has written the Chronicle with them since she began and buys every one that reaches the meadow. She has also written, at the front of each volume, in that same ink, that the entire book is being set down with a feather off an animal not one person in this country has ever seen, and that she wishes this noted. Under it, in a later hand: still no bird.

items.name: Watcher Eye
items.description: An eye that grew its own legs. It watched the whole fight from the floor, and it is still watching.
items.loreDesc: An eye that grew its own legs. It watched the whole fight from the floor, and it is still watching.

loreStory.t: Every stall that carries them carries a box with a lid, and the lid stays on while anyone at that stall is eating. Ask why and you get told bad luck, which is what the road says when it would rather not go into a thing. The plain reason is better. There are eight small eyes on the stalks and the big one in the middle, and they do not agree about where you are standing. A sorter works a bag for four hours at a stretch. Four hours is a long time to be got wrong by something on the table. Seventy-five gold, the dearest scrap off
the ringed mouth
that is not a stone, and every one of them travels face down.

items.name: Wing Quills
items.description: Three quills in blue, orange and gold, still bound together. Whatever wore them was worth looking at.
items.loreDesc: Three quills in blue, orange and gold, still bound together. Whatever wore them was worth looking at.

loreStory.t: Nothing wore all three. They are off three different somethings, and the binding is the item: a woman saw a bird once, alive, in a life she has otherwise let go of, and she has been matching its colours out of junk sacks ever since. The blue took four months. The orange is close and she knows it is not right. She brings them to
a fire
most weeks and describes the bird in order, one feather at a time, and has not yet reached the beak before the wood runs out.

items.name: Bone Bundle
items.description: Long pale bones tied off in a bundle. A Palehusk was carrying them, which raises questions about the string.
items.loreDesc: Long pale bones tied off in a bundle. A Palehusk was carrying them, which raises questions about the string.
loreStory: Fourteen gold for the bones, which is generous, and nothing whatever for the cord, which is the part everyone actually looks at.

loreStory.t: A
Palehusk

was carrying it. That is not the strange part — they carry things, and going through what a broken one leaves is reading rather than robbing. The strange part is the knot. A ropemaker on the black rock road was shown one and named it without hesitating: a load-hitch, thrown left over right and dressed down, the knot you use when you mean to carry a weight a long way and want it riding quiet on your back. It is not a knot a hand arrives at by accident. Somebody was taught it.

loreStory: The crackers untie them. They could cut them. They untie them.

items.name: Tooth Ridge
items.description: Ivory cones socketed in a slab of jawbone, unblunted. Whatever carried it never needed a second bite.
items.loreDesc: Ivory cones socketed in a slab of jawbone, unblunted. Whatever carried it never needed a second bite.

loreStory.t: The first thing a buyer does is run a thumb down the cones, and what he is checking is wear. Every other tooth that reaches a counter has been used — chipped, rounded, polished on the inner face where it met its opposite for years. A slab off
a Voidmaw
comes in with the enamel still ridged from growing. Every cone a first cone. The whole ridge unopened.

loreStory: Twenty-eight gold, and the price is not for the ivory. It is that a jaw which never wore is a jaw that never fed, and the crackers working that ground have turned it over more than they care to. Everything else out there is doing something you could put a reason to — hungry, cold, keeping a route, waiting at a gate that is not there any more. This one has never needed a thing in its life, and it is out there anyway.

items.name: Torn Wing
items.description: A small leathery wing, torn at the trailing edge. Something flies on these; nobody has cornered it yet.
items.loreDesc: A small leathery wing, torn at the trailing edge. Something flies on these; nobody has cornered it yet.

loreStory.t: Buyers want a pair. They always want a pair — one wing is an accident, two are a specimen — and in all the years of the trade not one honest pair has come in off the same creature. So the trade makes them. Take a big wing and a small one, trim the big one's trailing edge until the shapes agree, then rough the cut with a thumbnail so it reads as a tear. That is why so many torn wings are torn so tidily, and why a careful buyer holds the two edges up together and hunts for the same nick in both. Ten gold each, twenty-eight the pair, which tells you what the lie is worth. The whole point of
a pile of leavings
is that the details are still attached to it. This is the trade filing them off for eight gold, and the men who do it will tell you they are only giving people what they came in for.

items.name: Twig Skimmer
items.description: Four glassy wings over a body like a snapped twig. Shaken loose from whatever swamp thing you flattened.
items.loreDesc: Four glassy wings over a body like a snapped twig. Shaken loose from whatever swamp thing you flattened.

loreStory.t: The body is a stick. Not a figure of speech, and it is why the fraud is so easy: glue four wings onto
a twig

and you have twenty-two gold where you had five. Check the sockets. A real one carries four small raised collars in the shell, and you can find them with a thumbnail in the dark. Everybody in that market knows who makes the fakes. She is very good. Everybody buys hers anyway, because at twenty-two gold a fake with four real wings on it is still four real wings, and she has never once denied a thing.

items.name: Violet Shard
items.description: A wedge of violet crystal with a white heart. Snapped off Amethyrn's crown, which it will regrow.
items.loreDesc: A wedge of violet crystal with a white heart. Snapped off Amethyrn's crown, which it will regrow.
loreStory: It grows back, and that changed how it is taken. There is no sense breaking a shape that will hand you another wedge in two years, so the crown men break nothing: they come in at the shoulder while it feeds, tap once at the base with a wooden mallet, and walk out. Twice a decade, same animal. They call it husbandry and they are not entirely wrong.

loreStory.t: The bull

on the high pasture has been tapped nine times. It has started coming when the whistle goes. The young men take this as a compliment and tell it in company. The old ones have stopped drinking to it, because they know what it looks like when a thing keeps
walking a round
it no longer has any reason for, and this season they sent the young men up alone.

items.name: Violet Caps
items.description: Three violet caps still on their clod of earth. Mireback grows a crop of them across its shoulders.
items.loreDesc: Three violet caps on one root, the big one freckled pale. Turn it over before you pay for it.

loreStory.t: Everything you are buying is on the underside. Grown in ground, the base comes up dished and full of grit. Grown on an animal — on wet moss over a shoulder that has not moved through several winters — it comes up flat, and the stems all lean one way, downhill from where the withers were. Flat is worth triple. Flat also means the picker stood near enough to a
Mireback

to take three caps off it, which is a thing a person is entitled to be proud of, and is far more often a thing a person did at home with a board and a heavy stone. Buyers know. Sellers know they know. The haggling is two people agreeing not to say so.

items.name: Wheat Sheaf
items.description: Cut wheat bound at the waist, still smelling of a field that nobody has harvested in a long while.
items.loreDesc: Cut wheat bound at the waist, dry as paper. Somebody is still cutting a strip of that field every summer.

loreStory.t: The field grew itself, the way fields here do, out of a great many people being sure what a summer looks like. It does not need cutting. It is cut anyway, one strip a year along the north edge, by an old man with a scythe he made himself and has rehung twice. He binds at the waist, one turn and a tuck, and the collectors know his knot on sight and pay over the going rate for it, which he has never found out. Ask him why and he is perfectly clear: a field with nothing taken out of it looks wrong to him, and he would rather not look at it. He is not
thinning
. People who love him have asked, kindly, and he says so, and he is very probably right. Every year the strip is in the same place.

items.name: White Ribs
items.description: A full cage of ribs, bleached and oddly intact. It came out of something that stopped needing lungs.
items.loreDesc: A full cage of ribs, bleached and oddly intact. It came out of something that stopped needing lungs.
loreStory: Everything else on the counter is in pieces. That is what junk is — the bits that came apart. A cage comes off whole, spine and sternum and every rib still seated, and it stands up on the boards looking like the one intact thing in the room, and it will not sell that way.

loreStory.t: Sigrun

does the same thing every time. She looks at it, sets it on the floor, puts a boot through it, and pays the man the full price for it broken. She has never explained, the trade has stopped waiting for her to, and along that whole road it is simply how a cage is bought now. Twenty gold whole, twenty in pieces; the seller loses nothing, so everybody does it. Ask why and you get a shrug and four words. Because it was standing.

items.name: Worn Tusk
items.description: A short tusk ground flat on one side. Gnashjaw does that on purpose, to boulders, for hours.
items.loreDesc: A short tusk ground flat on one side. Gnashjaw does that on purpose, to boulders, for hours.
loreStory: The flat is the point. All that grinding leaves one face of the tusk as smooth as slate and about as willing to take a mark, and a scribe with a fine point and a steady hand can put a hundred words on one and know they will still be legible in three hundred years. Nothing else the trade handles will hold ink that long.

loreStory.t: Bettany

buys them and does not use them. Four sit blank on the shelf over her desk, bought at twenty-six gold apiece out of a purse that does not run to it. Asked why, she says she is saving them for names. Pressed at
Solveig
's fire on which names, she said the ones that are not going to be said out loud, and turned the talk to the weather, and has not been pressed again.

items.name: Worn Band
items.description: A plain band of dark wood banded in copper, sized for a finger that has stopped needing it.
items.loreDesc: A plain band of dark wood with a worn strip of metal let into it, sized for a finger that has stopped needing it.

loreStory.t: Wood, because metal was out of reach, and a band all the same. The strip let into it is a repair and not a decoration —
Osric

says it went on hot and shrank tight as it cooled, a smith's job properly done and properly charged for, and nobody pays a smith more than a ring is worth to save a ring. Somebody did. It came down off a
Grinmask

, and how it got there is a question the trade has settled by pricing it at twenty gold and moving on. Osric will not sell his. It has hung on a nail over his anvil eleven months, and when a cracker comes through the forge with another one he asks to see it, and turns it to the light, and looks at the repair rather than the ring, and hands it back without saying what he was hoping for.

items.name: Tooth Charm
items.description: A tooth bound in cord and hide, meant to be worn. The wrapping is careful; the tooth is not the wearer's.
items.waiting_for: a tribe that wears its kills
items.loreDesc: A tooth bound in cord and hide, meant to be worn. The wrapping is careful; the tooth is not the wearer's.
loreStory: Nine turns of cord, a hide collar cut to sit flat against the crown, a bead of amber set dead centre so it faces outward when the thing hangs. That is an evening's work, and it was not an evening spent on oneself: whoever took this tooth wrapped it up and handed it over, which is the exact opposite of what a trophy is for.

loreStory.t: After that it does the job all of them do. A stranger asks what it is. You tell them what it came off and where you were standing and who was standing with you, and they listen, because they asked first.
Bettany
has thirty-odd of these written into
the Chronicle

and not one of the entries is really about a tooth. Thirty gold at a counter buys you the object without the evening, and the trade knows perfectly well which half was worth having, and sells the other one anyway.

items.name: Slit Eye
items.description: A gold eye with a black slit, dry now. Emberjaw and its pale cousin both look at you out of these.
items.loreDesc: A gold eye with a black slit, dry now. Emberjaw and its pale cousin both look at you out of these.

loreStory.t: It comes out with the rim of skin still round it, because the eye on its own fetches half. The skin is the paper the sale is written on. Crusted, split, a seam of light gone dark in the crack, and it is off
the basking one
at the near end of the black rock. Olive going grey, dry, wrinkled flat, and it is off
the other
, which works ground a great deal closer to the mountain.

loreStory: So the eye prices the seller, not itself. There is a buyer at that end of the market who pays a shade over for the olive ones and keeps the tally in his head, and he knows to the month which crackers are still going out that far and which have quietly stopped. He has never said what the tally is for. He has twice sent somebody to sit at a crossing and wait for a man who was late.

items.name: Yellow Molar
items.description: Thumb-sized, yellowed and worn flat. Grinding teeth like this come out of things that chew all day.
items.loreDesc: Thumb-sized, yellowed and worn flat. Grinding teeth like this come out of things that chew all day.

loreStory.t: A horse sheds teeth the way any grazing thing does: the worn crown works loose and drops in the grass, and the animal goes on eating and never knows.
Solveig
found one at the edge of the firelight, on the line where
Snowmane

stops and turns and walks back out into the dark. It brings people in and it will not come in. She picked the tooth up and put it in her apron, and it has been in her apron since, and she is entirely clear about what it is not: it is not thanks, it is not a debt settled, and it does nothing whatever. It is worth twelve gold. It is hers. She keeps it where her hand goes.

items.name: Yellow Fang
items.description: A long fang gone yellow at the root and brown at the tip. Blightcur's whole jaw is full of them.
items.loreDesc: A long fang gone yellow at the root and brown at the tip. Blightcur's whole jaw is full of them.

loreStory.t: Twelve gold, and the yellow is not age — it comes up that colour on a jaw that has never been any other. A
Blightcur

's leavings cost a bright shape nothing worse than a foul week and a taste of old metal. What they cost somebody already thinning is far more than the fang is worth. Everyone knows it. It is not said aloud at a market, ever.

loreStory: So the yellow lot lies open with the cheap stock, where every hand in the place goes through it, and the traders watch for the hand that stops. It is not done to be cruel. When a hand stops, the trader finds something to be doing at that end of the stall, and talks, and keeps talking, and by the second visit there is a stool out. Half the fires on that road were told who to go and sit with by a man selling teeth.

items.name: Soulstone
items.description: Violet facets around a gold rune, cut from an Emberwing. Hits land arcane, and spells come back to hand faster.

soul.power: +20 arcane damage on hit and -10% spell cooldowns

items.loreDesc: Faceted violet, plum deepening to lilac, with a thumbnail of gold at the middle that looks written rather than grown.

loreStory.t: Every facet on one is a one-off; the mark is not. Two strokes and a splayed foot, in gold, small enough to hide under a thumbnail, identical down to the stroke on every stone ever brought in. Off a creature that is
nothing but retellings

, the piece that pressed hardest was the one thing all its tellers' countries remember alike: gold, which does not drift. Set in a blade it lends tempo — the stroke arrives as if it had been made once already.
The mark is also why it is the most forged stone on any bench. Violet glass lumps well, and a forger with real gold gets the mark right every time, gold being the point of gold.
Osric
, new enough to still count in living years, bought one cheap off a stranger at his first market and carried it to
Sigrun

for setting. She drew it once through her hearth ash and handed it back grey. Ash will not sit on a true one — one wipe and it is finished — and the glass kept its coat. It hangs over his forge door now with the price scratched underneath, and he takes the ribbing better than he would take the sympathy.

items.name: Soulstone
items.description: Dark banded stone lined with living gold, pulled from a Glowbone. Burns with light, and nearby undead go blind.

soul.power: +20 radiant damage on hit and blinds undead within three tiles

items.loreDesc: Dark stone terraced in bands, a seam of live gold running the length of them. It lights whatever pouch you put it in.
loreStory: The smiths' rule with this one: never on the bench after dark. The seam is live, and beside heated metal there is no telling the colour of the work from the colour coming off the stone, so settings happen at noon with the doors open, by people who otherwise keep their doors shut to read the heat.

loreStory.t: It does not go down when you put it away, which is why you cannot carry one and also arrive anywhere unannounced — and why, when the fire on the east road lapsed, its last keeper left a banded stone glowing on the sill as she went, so the road would think the light was still kept.
Wendell

walked that road while the trick still worked. He says you could tell a mile off, because a fire moves and a stone only glows. He stopped anyway, both ways, sat down on the step, and told it what he had seen on the road lately. It seemed wrong to pass a kept light without paying for it.
What bothers people is that it lends the whole light, undiminished, out of a lump a hand closes around. As if
the creature it comes off
was never lit through at all — as if the light was always this small, and the body was built around it for carrying.

items.name: Soulstone
items.description: Charred black, cracked open by molten veins. Magmashell's banked fire, and it leaves what you hit burning.

soul.power: +14 fire damage on hit and sets targets burning for 3s

items.loreDesc: Charred black plates forked open by live orange veins that never cool. What you strike goes on burning after you stop.
loreStory: Ask somebody who carries one what they carry it in and you get a considered answer. Cloth chars through in a season; a pouch comes back stiff as a boot dried too near the hearth. Most end at a tin of sand lashed outside the pack, where the thing that cannot be persuaded to stop can do the least.

That is also what it does off an edge. Most fire is over when the swing is; this one is left behind, still burning after you step back. What got pressed to make it was never flame — it was the banking: heat held in, year after year, no fuel, no audience, no occasion. A thing like that does not learn to finish just because you have.

loreStory.t: Few ever come to hand, since a crossing has to empty first, and the one
Magmashell
anyone can still visit shows no sign of obliging. A collector once offered
Gunnar

good gold to stop paying its pause — one regular fewer, one crossing nearer done. Gunnar quoted back the number of years he has walked it, and the collector could not tell whether that was a price or a warning. Neither has anyone since.

items.name: Soulstone
items.description: Black shell split by wide lava rivers, out of a Basalthowl. When it roars the mountain answers.

soul.power: +20 fire damage on hit, and a kill sets everything nearby burning

items.loreDesc: Black shell split by wide lava rivers running to a white-hot centre. Nothing goes down beside it on its own.

loreStory.t: The burnt country gives up two stones and a dealer does not need a glass to sort them. The common one,
off a pack wolf
, runs its veins narrow and dark red. This one has rivers in it a thumb wide, and where they meet the colour goes past orange into white. There is one such animal to a pack, and the price says so.
Osric

grades them the way only a smith would think to. He leaves the stone on the anvil overnight and puts a hand flat on the iron in the morning. A pack stone leaves the anvil cold. This kind warms two feet of it. He has never had a true one fail that, and he has been brought a good many that did.

loreStory: He sets them into other people's blades all week and will not have one in his own hearth. Customers get a reason about wood bills. What he does not tell them is what the stone does at the moment something goes down beside it, which is that everything nearby catches — grass, ground, whatever else was still standing. It is not burning to be burning. It is burning so that nothing near it goes down by itself. He arrived here wanting a hearth that fed itself, and he has one on the bench, priced, and he does not sit with it in the evenings.

items.name: Soulstone
items.description: Blue-grey and plated like something forged, taken off an Ironhide. Spears skate off it exactly the same.

soul.power: +18 armor, and piercing weapons lose a third of their damage against you

items.loreDesc: Blue-grey and plated like something forged, taken off an Ironhide. Spears skate off it exactly the same.
loreStory: It has no flat face. That is the first thing any setter says about it: blue-grey plates laid over one another with a pale seam at every join, so that wherever you put the tool you are putting it on a lid. The answer is a cup rather than a bezel, four claws and a bed, seated by feel. It never shifts afterwards. The plates take the pressure sideways and hand it round the stone, which is more or less what they do to a spear.

In armour it pays out against points. A thrust that should have opened a seam arrives instead as a shove, the arm goes numb to the elbow, and the day continues. Every wearer describes it the same way and none of them calls it strength: they say they were pushed rather than reached.

loreStory.t: The animal

will not hold still to be looked at. You can stand off a hundred paces and watch it breathe all afternoon and still not know whether those bands were grown or worn. Break the shape and the argument ends in the grass: what falls out is plated too, all the way to the bottom, seams and all, with no buckle-gap anywhere a harness would have to leave. It was not wearing anything.
Sigrun
keeps one on the shelf above her bench, unset, the only stone in that forge she has never taken a hammer to. It is not stock. It is the answer, and she has not finished reading it.

items.name: Soulstone
items.description: Blue slate cracked around a cold white star, pulled from a Winterfang. It frosts a blade and drags at its target.

soul.power: +9 frost damage and slows struck targets by 25%

items.loreDesc: Blue slate cracked around a cold white star, pulled from a Winterfang. It frosts a blade and drags at its target.
loreStory: It comes out of the grass warm. They all do — you find a stone in the dark by heat and not by shape, and that is the first thing anyone learns at a bench. This one is warm for about an hour. Then it is not, and it never is again. Crackers working the frost country know the hour and spend it: one walk home with the thing warm in the glove, and after that a cold weight in a tin that stays cold in a hot room and will not take heat back off anything you set it against.

What it does to a fight is mostly not damage. It is the drag. A struck thing does not stagger and does not go down, it only arrives late for everything it meant to do next, and keeps arriving late, and a fight against something a quarter slow stops being a fight and turns into arithmetic. Setters will put one in a blade and will not put one in a haft, for reasons your hand works out inside ten minutes.

loreStory.t: A drawing of
Winterfang

gives you the crown of ice, the icicles off the jaw, the claws standing out white, and tells you the animal is cold. It cannot tell you what the cold cost, because the animal will not come near enough to be asked and would not answer. The stone answers. An hour of warm and then nothing, for good, whatever it is held against — that is the trade the creature made and the side of it that it lost, sitting in a tin on a bench for anyone to pick up. Keepers who have had one of those standing at the rim of their light all night do not much enjoy hearing this said out loud.

items.name: Soulstone
items.description: Blue-grey plates around a white star. Cold to hold, and nothing anyone has killed was carrying it.

soul.power: +10 frost damage on hit, and cold targets take 15% more

items.loreDesc: Blue-grey plates around a white star. Cold to hold, and nothing anyone has ever broken was carrying it.

loreStory.t: Grading is done by hand and mostly in the dark, because a grader who works by eye starts trusting colour, and colour is the least of what a stone is. The hands learn heft and warmth and the width of a seam. One tray to a kind of creature, and
the rule underneath that
has never yet failed.

loreStory: This one is cold. Not cool — cold, the way a pebble out of a beck is cold, and it stays that way in a shut hand, so the hand has it before the eye has done anything at all. Blue-grey plates, a white star sunk in the middle, ninety gold. In a haft it bites frost, hardest at whatever is cold already.

The grader on the north bench keeps a tray with nothing else in it. She has been told to file them in with the crystal country's stones — same weight, same setting, same buyers — and she will not, and her reason is not an argument: those came off something, she has held them, this is not one of those. Her trays are named for creatures. That one has no name over it, and she keeps it standing so that if a name ever turns up she will know which stones to move. Six in it, over nineteen years. The other benches call that superstition and file theirs under frost with the rest — and every grader on every one of those benches can pick the odd stone out of a frost tray by touch, in the dark, first try.

items.name: Soulstone
items.description: Bright green plates with black seams, alive-looking. Its creature is still somewhere in the deep wood.

soul.power: +12 nature damage on hit, and poisons on you end twice as fast

items.loreDesc: Bright green plates with black seams, alive-looking. Its creature is still somewhere in the deep wood.
loreStory: Four or five come in a season, always off the deep-wood roads, always the same stone: bright green plates, seams gone nearly black, the whole of it wet-looking in a dry hand. It sells the day it lands. Everything in that wood bites and most of it is worse an hour later, and a piece that finishes a poison in half the time it would have taken is worth a hundred and fifteen gold to anyone who works in there, and more to anyone who has been carried out of it once already.

loreStory.t: What the trade cannot do with it is the ordinary thing.
People who crack shapes for a living

keep books — the shape, the ground, the morning, who swung — because that is how they are paid and how they settle arguments, and every other stone on a bench can be walked back along one of them. This one is in nobody's book. Every seller of one bought it from a seller; run the chain back and it goes three or four hands and stops — at a road, at a fire that is not kept any more, at a man who has moved on and cannot be produced.

loreStory: So the sellers say its creature is still out there in the deep wood, and it is a good line, and it costs nothing, and it may well be true. It is also an answer to a question that was not asked. Where the creature is has never been the difficulty here. Where the stones are coming from is.

items.name: Soulstone
items.description: Dull brown plates veined with copper, left by a Puddling. Thickens armor and roots you where you stand.

soul.power: +12 armor and 15% knockback resistance

items.loreDesc: Dull brown plates shut on a copper vein, far too heavy for its size. A Puddling's last piece; in armour, hard to shift.
loreStory: The one they put in a new hand first. It weighs wrong — not heavy, wrongly heavy, in a way the arm reports before the eye agrees. Armour set with one does the same trick at scale: the blow that should have put you on your back leaves you standing where you were, and you find out afterwards. Wearers call it the least dramatic advantage in the trade, and keep wearing it.

loreStory.t: The trouble is the count. Every hard piece is supposed to be
the bottom of one long forgetting
, and the wet ground gives up more of these than the low country has lives to account for, by a margin that worsens every season.
Wendell
says that in his day the count came out even. Wendell says that about most counts.

loreStory: The sorters keep three explanations in stock. That the ground itself is doing the forgetting, and the wet places are where it runs deepest. That the counting was always sloppy. And a third, said late in the evening and not repeated in daylight: that the arithmetic is fine, and it is the assumption of one life to one stone that is wrong.

items.name: Soulstone
items.description: Brown stone with a wood grain and two dark knots. Nothing that grows has been caught carrying one.

soul.power: +10 armor, and fire does 15% less to you

items.loreDesc: Brown stone with a wood grain and two dark knots. Nothing that grows has been caught carrying one.
loreStory: It is not a rare stone. That is the whole of the difficulty. A collector three months in owns one, because they are cheap and they keep turning up, and any dealer with a bench has two or three under the cloth. It passes every test the trade has: warm within a breath of the hand, no chip under a bench hammer, pale glassy seams that take a setting cleanly. In a plate it does what it promises — the blow arrives smaller, and fire arrives smaller still, which is the joke every buyer makes about a stone with a grain in it, and the joke is most of why they sell.

loreStory.t: By
the rule of the thing

, one kind of creature leaves one kind of stone. Nothing that grows has ever been broken carrying one of these. Not a standing shape out of the black wood, not a root thing out of the fen, nothing anybody has ever put a bag under.
Gunnar

has walked more of this country than the rest of them together and keeps what he measures to himself. Somebody asked him straight, at the fire, in front of people, whether he had ever in his life seen a thing of wood get up and go anywhere. He said no. He was asked whether that settled it. He said it settled where he had been.

items.name: Soulstone
items.description: Packed grey-green cobbles, unlit as fen water. A Bogstalker's own — blows slide past you, worse in the mist.

soul.power: +8% dodge chance and attackers miss more often in dim light

items.loreDesc: Packed grey-green cobbles, unlit as fen water. A Bogstalker's own — blows slide past you, worse in the mist.
loreStory: It is the one stone in the trade where a shine counts against it. Grade it in a dark room with a single candle at arm's length: a good one gives the candle back nothing at all, packed grey-green cobbles with a dark seam at every join and no face anywhere for light to sit on. A poor one has a highlight somewhere, and a highlight can be aimed at. Those go for half, and they go quickly, because they are still beautiful and beauty sells to people who have not crossed anything.

loreStory.t: Fen-walkers already own the other half of this trick, rolled up on the end of a pole. What thinned out of
the cat

was not hunger; the last thing to go was the moment of committing, the certainty that the outline in the water is the one. Carry a piece of somebody else's certainty and everything aimed at you comes in slightly wrong. You are not hidden. You are only not quite the shape the blow was meant for, and in mist, where nothing has an edge, it was not really meant for anyone in particular.

loreStory: There is a rule about buying one and it is nowhere in writing. You do not buy your own. A walker gets his from another walker at the end of a good season, handed over on the bank without ceremony, and a man who buys his own has told the whole ford something about his plans. They will take his gold. They will also stop working the far side with him.

items.name: Soulstone
items.description: Cream stone with a warm gold star at its heart, left by Sorrel. It still knows the way to the gate.

soul.power: +12% movement speed, and you tire slower under a full pack

items.loreDesc: Cream stone with a warm gold star at its heart, left by Sorrel. It still knows the way to the gate.
loreStory: Fifty-five gold, which is nothing, and it is on every carrier walking every road between fires. Cream, softly mottled, a gold burst low and off-centre in the heart of it like a lit window seen across a field. What it does is unglamorous and worth more than stones costing five times as much: your feet keep the last hour of a long day as though it were the third, and a full pack stops being an argument you are having with yourself. In a fight it is worth precisely nothing.

loreStory.t: Graders say what is at the bottom of it flatly, because it is not a mystery. Not speed. The willingness to do the whole day again tomorrow.
Sorrel

is remembered for standing at a gate at dusk waiting to be brought in, and the standing is what people walk out to look at — but a stone is a fairer record of a life than the picture anybody carries of it. What went all the way down was not the waiting. It was the coming back up the slope, every evening, for however many years it has been now.
Bettany

wears one and does not pretend it is for the walking: she carries paper and ink out to people who are thinning, she is losing that race by about one person a season, and the stone gets her as far as the next one.

items.name: Soulstone
items.description: Crimson with one spiral rune cut deep. Unclaimed: nothing that bleeds has dropped it so far.

soul.power: Heal 10% of damage dealt while below half health

items.loreDesc: Crimson with one spiral rune cut deep. Unclaimed: nothing that bleeds has dropped it so far.

loreStory.t: Nothing happens while you are winning, which is the difficulty in selling one: the only demonstration is a bad afternoon. Below your half it starts paying, a tenth of everything you land coming back the other way, for exactly as long as you are losing. Above that line it is a heavy red pebble worth two hundred and twenty
gold
. Whatever settled to the bottom of it had no interest in a fight until the fight was going badly.
The spiral goes in deep and was not cut. The trade had that argument already over
a stone with a frost-rune in it
and will not have it twice: a few come up with a shape in them, the shape runs all the way down, and there is no bench mark on any of them.

loreStory: There is a buyer who pays three hundred. He has paid it eleven times, to eleven sellers, in weighed gold, and has never once haggled, which in this trade is stranger than the money. The seller who asked what he wanted them for was told it was a fair price, and asked whether he would like it. He would. Nothing that bleeds has ever been broken carrying one — it is the first thing anybody says about the stone, and he knows it better than the people telling him. He is buying them faster than they surface, and there is not one under a cloth on any bench in the country tonight.

items.name: Soulstone
items.description: Mossy green split by a red vein, cut from a Stumpling. It hits harder and feeds the wound back to you.

soul.power: +9 damage on hit and heals you for 8% of damage dealt

items.loreDesc: Moss green blotched with bark brown, dark veins branching in to one red knot at the middle. Filed with the blood stones.
loreStory: In a full bag you can find one without looking. Every hard piece is warm; this one is warm unevenly, a hot spot over the red knot at the middle, the way heat comes through a coat with somebody in it. Collectors mention that to each other exactly once, at the start, and not again.

loreStory.t: Every one of these on a bench was cracked out of
a Stumpling
by a hand other than
Sigrun's

; her refusal is its own story. What her bench shows is the other half of it: she will set the stones once the cracking is done elsewhere — sets them better than anyone in the district — and she lifts each one from the tray with the long tongs she otherwise keeps for iron out of the fire.

loreStory: An apprentice asked about the tongs once, it being a cold stone by iron's standards. It is warm in the middle, she said. They are all warm, said the apprentice, which is true. Not like this, she said, and got on with the setting, and the apprentice put the question away with the other things you do not ask Sigrun twice.

items.name: Soulstone
items.description: Plated grey rock split by a bright cyan seam of Rimeshard ice. In a blade it bites deep frost and leaves the target wading.

soul.power: +16 frost damage on hit and slows the target by 30% for 3 seconds

items.loreDesc: Grey plates split by one bright cyan seam that runs clean through. It bites frost, and what it strikes runs late.

loreStory.t: Warm, which is the first surprise — off the crystal ground, out of a shape that is ice from the crown down, and it sits in the palm at blood heat, the seam warmest of all. The sorters point to that when asked whether anything in a
Rimeshard
was ever under way at all: watched from a ridge it might as well be weather, and weather does not leave a warm stone.

loreStory: The grading is done on the seam, not on either material. Sight along it: on a good one the cyan enters one face and comes out the other, clean through. On a poor one it stops inside, and what you own is a grey pebble with a stripe. The rock alone is worth nothing; the ice alone is worth nothing; the join is the worth.

loreStory.t: New hands find that funny for about a week.
Osric

did not laugh at all. He is a smith; a join that outvalues both its pieces was the first price in this country that struck him as honestly arrived at, and he paid it without haggling, which the stone-sellers still bring up.

items.name: Soulstone
items.description: Pebbled black stone veined in cyan, the storm inside a Frostwraith. Its lightning strikes, then jumps to the next body.

soul.power: +15 lightning damage with a 20% chance to chain to a second target

items.loreDesc: Pebbled black under a net of branching cyan that will not sit still. Warm. Its spark rarely stops at one body.

loreStory.t: In the graders' register, the ground a stone comes off and the nature it grades to are two columns saying one thing — black rock, fire; high snow, frost. This is the line where the columns disagree: it comes down off
the Frostwraith
's snow, many days uphill, and it grades storm.
Gunnar
brings most of them down. He sells the stones readily and the places he found them not at all, which people take for a wanderer's habit, and which is actually arithmetic he does not like.

They fetch more than anything else off that mountain, and the first thing anyone learns fighting with one is not to let a friend stand at their shoulder: the spark goes where it is sent, and then sometimes it is in the next body along, whichever body that is.
Sigrun

will set one — for the price they carry she can hardly refuse — but she asks a single question first, who do you fight beside, and there are answers she hands the stone back over. Asked for her reasoning, she taps the head of her hammer and does not give it.

items.name: Soulstone
items.description: Pale blue lit by cyan forks, grown in a Voltshell's crystals. Thunder rolls a long way behind it.

soul.power: Lightning strikes attackers for 15, and storms never slow you

items.loreDesc: Pale blue lit by cyan forks, grown in a Voltshell's crystals. Thunder rolls a long way behind it.

loreStory.t: No other stone is sold with an address.
The animal

walks one line at a known pace and does not turn aside, so a seller can hand a buyer a field and a month and still be right about it a year later. They sell the field separately from the stone, and nobody has ever called that greedy, because there is no other errand in this country you can promise a man in advance.

loreStory: Two hundred and eighty-five gold, top of most sheets, and the forked cyan is not what holds the price. Plenty of stones bite back at whoever hits you. It is the second half. While that stone is on you the weather stops being an argument you are having — sleet, headwind, a sky doing whatever it likes — and the pace you finish the day at is the pace you set out at. On roads that take a week, in a country where the road may be somewhere else next month, arriving is worth a fortune.

The fetching is reckoned an easy day's work and it is, and the trade says so without listening to the shape of its own sentence. It will not turn aside for weather, or for a valley going soft, or for the crew walking out to break it open, and there is no account of one ever being surprised. What is at the bottom of that shell was never the storm; the storm was always the sky's business, borrowing the crystals. It is the line. Everything hard about the errand is the walking, and the walking is weeks.

items.name: Soulstone
items.description: Woodgrain runs black through it, all a felled Sprigling leaves. It hardens armor and hands blows back to the giver.

soul.power: +8 armor and 5% of damage taken is reflected to the attacker

items.loreDesc: Dark as bog oak, black grain running through the brown. A felled Sprigling's last: it stiffens plate and hands blows back.
loreStory: It will not take a polish and it will not be forced. There is grain in it, black under the brown, turning at a knot the way sawn oak turns, and an armourer sets a plate across the run of it or watches the first real blow start a split that does not stop. No other stone asks to be read first. Most of the trade finds that quietly insulting.

Worn right, it keeps a ledger: a share of every blow goes back to whoever gave it, at once, at about the size it was given, and the wearer feels nothing at all. Two exchanges in, the other party is usually looking at their own hands. Not protection — bookkeeping.

loreStory.t: Osric

ruined his first one the week he bought it, taking a smith's hammer to a thing that wanted a joiner's patience, and the two halves are nailed up over his forge door. Ask why he keeps them and you get the whole of what he will so far say about being dead: some things here are worked with, not on. Then he reads the next
Sprigling
stone a long while before touching it, like a man laying a floor.

items.name: Soulstone
items.description: Dark green with one bright eye of light at its centre. Mireglare's stare, still lit, still looking.

soul.power: Hits burn for 8 over 4 seconds, and burning targets cannot hide from you

items.loreDesc: Dark green with one bright eye of light at its centre. Mireglare's stare, still lit, still looking.
loreStory: The test for a real one is barely a test. Shut your fist on it in a dark room and there is still a green line between your fingers. Every other hard piece is a habit or an appetite pressed down until it is very nearly mineral, and mineral does not do anything. This one is lit. Lit is the wrong word for a stone and the trade uses it anyway, having no better.

What it does in a fight follows from what it is. It does not find anything for you. It marks one thing, and after that the thing cannot get out of your sight by stepping out of it — not behind a bank, not into the reeds. The attention does not come off. Fen hunters say the unpleasant part is how quickly you stop bothering to look.

loreStory.t: The fen keeps a long vocabulary for what
the stare

is supposed to do to a person, and none of it is true; the animal is only working through faces. The stone settles a harder question, and settles it badly: break the shape, pick the piece out of the grass, and the checking is still going. It went all the way down and it did not finish.
Bettany

keeps hers on the desk, facing the room. She will not shut a thing that is still looking into a drawer, and she has written in her own margin that she cannot say whether that is courtesy or superstition.

items.name: Soulstone
items.description: Black stone with a red star burning at the core, pulled out of a Rotjaw. It refuses to stay dead too.

soul.power: Once per fight, a blow that would kill you leaves you standing on one hit point instead

items.loreDesc: Near-black, veined dark red around a red star at the core, out of a Rotjaw. It will not let you go down either.

loreStory.t: Forty-two gold: the cheapest useful stone in the country, for the one service no seller has ever managed to price honestly. The arithmetic behind the discount is not pretty.
The animal

stands where the hill tracks begin to climb, it does not run, and it will still be standing there next season. Common is the whole of the reason. Every bag-carrier on the hill roads has one and most of them have never found out whether it works.

loreStory: It is near-black, veined dark red under the surface like something that has not gone out, with a small red star at the middle brighter than any part of a stone should be. It fires once. A blow that was going to put you down does not, and you are on your feet with nothing left but the standing, and the beat you have been handed is short and yours to do something with. People it has happened to report the same odd thing afterwards, never the one you expect. Not that they survived. That the end arrived and then declined to become the next moment.

loreStory.t: Jehanne

keeps a bowl of them inside her door and puts one into the hand of anyone leaving her fire for a road, and takes nothing for it. She does not promise them it works. She does not tell them it will not. She has been carrying out a practice she stopped believing in for longer than most of them have been in the world, and the only defence of the bowl she has ever offered is that a forty-gold stone is at least a thing you can put in somebody's hand.

items.name: Soulstone
items.description: Dark teal plates, always beaded with water. The thing that grew it has not surfaced yet.

soul.power: +10% swim speed, and you breathe underwater

items.loreDesc: Dark teal plates, always beaded with water. The thing that grew it has not surfaced yet.
loreStory: Grading is comparison. You hold the stone against the creature — that is the entire method, and it works, because one kind of creature leaves one kind of stone and the trade has spent a long time pairing them off. There is nothing to hold this one against. So the graders read it backwards instead, out of what it does, and every one of them arrives at the same sentence and none of them enjoy saying it aloud: whatever reached the bottom of this had no particular reason to come up.

It is heavy for its size and plated like something's back, overlapping dark teal with a bright seam at every edge, warm as any stone in the trade and beaded all over with water it has no business having. Worn, you swim like a thing that lives down there. And you breathe. Not hold your breath longer — breathe, for as long as you care to, which is the part sellers say twice.

loreStory.t: Gunnar

uses one for work. A Turn put four miles of the low road under water eleven years ago and he has walked the whole of it since, along the bottom, correcting a map he has not been asked for. He has said one thing about the stone, to one person, and it had nothing to do with the map: down there he does not think about breathing at all, and twice he has come up only because the light went, and he could not afterwards say how long he had been under. He does not speculate about what grew it. He has noticed what it does to a man only borrowing the habit, and he has gone back down anyway.

items.name: Soulstone
items.description: Deep red, cracked like drying blood. Whatever it came out of has not been brought down yet.

soul.power: +12 damage against wounded targets, and heals 5% of it back

items.loreDesc: Deep red plates with every crack lit orange to a hot centre. Whatever it came out of has not been brought down yet.
loreStory: Every other stone on a bench is in the past tense. A stone is what is left when a shape comes apart; the shape is accounted for, the creature is a matter of record, and the whole vocabulary runs that way — released, cracked, brought in. This one is sold with a tense the trade does not otherwise use. Not yet, said flatly, the way you would say a thing about scheduling.

A hundred gold, and not a fighting stone. Against anything still whole it does nothing worth the setting; against something already opened it adds twelve and hands you back a twentieth. The graders go this far and no further, and they say it as a description of the stone and of nothing else: what reached the bottom here was not hunger and was not endurance. It was a preference for things that had already begun to lose.

loreStory.t: Then the arithmetic, which everybody does once and drops. Nineteen have come in that anyone can put a name to.
One kind of creature, one kind of stone

— so nineteen stones are nineteen shapes broken, by hands, at some hour, in some country, and not one of those hands has ever sat down at a fire and said so. Either it is being done quietly, which is not how crackers are; a good story is half the wage. Or the first rule anybody learns has a hole in it the exact size of this stone.

items.name: Soulstone
items.description: Dark red with an orange star bursting through the cracks. Cinderhowl is cracked open the same way.

soul.power: +12 fire damage on hit, and the target burns for 5 a second

items.loreDesc: Dark red with an orange star bursting through the cracks. Cinderhowl is cracked open the same way.
loreStory: Every hard piece comes out warm. This one comes out hot at the middle and stays there, so it travels in a tin, lashed to the outside of the pack. Every dealer says so to every new buyer, and every second one finds out the other way regardless. There are men on the west road who will show you the hole in the lining before you have asked.

loreStory.t: Most of them go to
the rotas

rather than to the fights. A keeper on a wet round can shove one under sodden kindling, walk off to see to somebody, and come back to a fire. It does not want dry, or shelter, or nursing, and it will do it again tomorrow night and in four hundred years, and seventy-two gold for that is not a price, it is a gift. Half the western keepers who still hold a rota worth the name have one, and treat it exactly like a kettle.
What the people who fetch them will not do is set one in a blade.
The hound

leaves its work still going on behind it, embers putting themselves out in the grass a long while after it has gone by, and a stone is the bottom of the kind, so that is what you have bought: the hit lands, and then it goes on landing, while you stand there. The trade rests on two words and both of them describe one blow. Ask a cracker why he keeps his in a tin and you get a shrug, or you get the honest answer, which is that he does not want to be given the time to change his mind.

items.name: Soulstone
items.description: Green stone cracked with pale light, off a Mireback. Mushrooms fruit on it if you leave it alone.

soul.power: Heal 6% of the damage you deal, and twice that standing in water

items.loreDesc: Green stone cracked with pale light, off a Mireback. Mushrooms fruit on it if you leave it alone.
loreStory: Shut one in a bag for a week and there are pinheads in the seams. Leave it a month and they are red-caps, small and entirely ordinary, fruiting on a mineral that has no business feeding anything. Wipe them off and they come again. Nothing else out of a broken shape does this, and most sellers polish before a viewing and say nothing about it, which is how the dyed ones got as far as they did.

For the better part of a decade a man worked the fen circuit with pale stones soaked green, priced a third under, and a story about the swamp being poor ground to collect in. He was right about the ground. Three buyers worked out what they had and told their fires, and it went on anyway, because the fakes showed better than the true ones — brighter, cleaner, nothing rotting in the seams.

loreStory.t: It ended over a bag. A dealer asked to see the bag and not the stone, and the bag was clean, and every honest
Mireback
stone stains its cloth. That is the grading now: you are not buying the stone, you are buying the mark it left on the lining.

loreStory: What it pays out is not protection. The work comes back to you as fast as you do it, and comes back double standing in water. A wood bear whose wood went four feet under did not stop walking its round when the ground changed its mind. Neither does the piece at the bottom of it.

items.name: Soulstone
items.description: Sea-green stone mended in gold, prised from a Palemaw's jaw. Armor holds better, and more coin turns up.

soul.power: +15% gold found and +6 armor

items.loreDesc: Sea-green, webbed with gold where it broke and broke again. It holds armour together, and gold has a way of turning up.
loreStory: Gold in the hand is always cold. The gold in this one is exactly as warm as the sea-green around it, and that detail still stops conversations. The mend is no setting, either: it runs the whole way through, filed and worked like trade goldwork, and it will not come out of the stone, nor the stone off it.

Handlers grade by the seams and argue the count — one school calls it a tally of seasons worked, the other says a stone is not a calendar. What the count means is not argued: this broke, and held, and broke again, and held. Armourers promise only that a plate carrying one comes apart later than it should, and often not at all. A stone that is mostly mend teaches a mend.

loreStory.t: Halvard
, the pedlar who walks his pack between the fires and
prices in nothing but gold
, will buy one, sell one, carry one — and book it as stone, never as gold: gold that cannot be spent is not gold to him. Pressed once, he weighed a
Palemaw

stone in his palm, said the difference between the two prices was the animal, and would not be drawn further. He does allow that carriers find more gold in a season than luck explains, and he counts his purse twice after trading with one.

items.name: Soulstone
items.description: Gold-cased and cut with a sunburst rune, left by a Runemane. It is still carrying out old orders.

soul.power: +20 radiant damage on hit, and every fifth strike blocks the next blow against you

items.loreDesc: Gold-cased and cut with a sunburst rune, left by a Runemane. It is still carrying out old orders.
loreStory: The two who brought the first one in could not agree, that night at the fire, on what they had done. One of them used the polite word and said released. The other would not take either of the trade's two words and kept saying, instead, that they had taken a fitting off a building.

loreStory.t: He had the better of it and everybody knew.
The guardian

is Made: it never fell and was never anywhere, only remembering that pooled with nothing to be, thickened, and stood up at a door. A stone is the last hard piece of somebody, the bottom of a long forgetting, and there is not supposed to be a bottom to a thing that was never filled. Yet here it lies in its gold case, warm as any of them, the sunburst still lit in the cut of it, doing what it plainly does: set it in a blade and every fifth strike, unasked and without fail, it puts itself in front of the next blow. It is not protecting you. It is standing where it was told to stand.
They left it at the meadow fire and went, which is what people do with a thing they cannot price.
Solveig

has had it in her apron since. Somebody there made the obvious comparison out loud, in the tone people use when they think they are being kind — the last one on a rota that lapsed everywhere else. She said the lion was left with orders and she was left with people, and that these are not the same thing, and got up to see to the wood.

items.name: Soulstone
items.description: Cobbled grey rock leaking the green that kept a Palehusk walking. In a weapon its poison layers wound on wound.

soul.power: +13 poison damage on hit stacking up to five times

items.loreDesc: Cobbled grey plates, green standing wet in every joint. In a blade the poison layers on and never clears out.
loreStory: It travels alone, at the bottom of the bag, with something folded between it and the rest, because the green gets out — not much, never fast, never stopping. A pouch that has carried one for a season is marked inside for good. The crackers' rule is flat: you carry one of these, or you carry the rest.

loreStory.t: So somebody has to walk the green bag, and the somebody is
Jehanne

. She took the office unasked, the way she takes every office no one else wants, and walks a day behind the buying party with the bag on a pole over her shoulder, washing her hands at every stream, saying over each stone the blessing of a faith she tells everyone she no longer holds. The trade pays her in firewood. She has never once been robbed.
Graders can usually say inside a minute whether the thing in their hand is a fact, an appetite, or a habit. This one is none of the three. It is a substance — the same green
the Palehusk
leaks — and a substance is not a life pressed small. It grades high anyway. High enough that the question rarely gets asked twice.

items.name: Soulstone
items.description: Grey-brown and split by dark seams, ground smooth. Gnashjaw wears its tusks down on rock like this.

soul.power: Hits grind through armor, stripping 8 armor from the target for 6 seconds

items.loreDesc: Grey-brown and split by dark seams, ground smooth. Gnashjaw wears its tusks down on rock like this.

loreStory.t: Osric

has patched the same coat of mail three times for the same customer and finally said it across the counter: it is not cutting your mail, it is using it. A stone like this does not hit hard. It takes a little armour off, hands it back a breath later, takes a little more — and a man carrying one who simply keeps coming at you all afternoon will have the whole coat by evening. Forty-five gold. Every second beginner owns one, and the few who learn patience early keep it for years.
Go and watch
Gnashjaw

and you will see an animal filing its own tusks flat on a boulder, and you will call it tooth-care, because that is what it looks like and because the other reading takes some sitting with. The stone will not leave you the comfortable one. Pale grey lobes in rust-dark seams, the whole face worn flat and glossy, warm in the hand: what refused to thin any further in that creature was not the teeth, and was not the strength either. It was the wearing away. An animal can keep what its life is about to itself for as long as you care to stand there looking at it. A stone cannot, and every dealer between here and the east country has held one, and the young ones are out there grinding tonight.

items.name: Soulstone
items.description: Grey plates shut around a clot of Duskfang red. It sharpens a weapon and feeds part of every wound back to you.

soul.power: +6 damage and heals for 15% of damage dealt

items.loreDesc: Cold grey plates with a warm red seam shut inside them. It gives nothing until you cut, and then it takes its share back.
loreStory: Buyers turn one to the light, hunting the gap where the red shows through. The crackers gave that habit up years ago — shut tight or on show, it is the same stone — and test with the fist instead: close it and wait for one warm line to come up against the palm, in a stone otherwise colder than the grass it came out of.

What it does begins half a breath after your first cut lands. Whatever you opened, some part of it comes back the other way and closes what it finds. Everyone who has felt it says the same two things in the same order: that it is a great deal of comfort, and that it is not a kindness. Nothing is being given. Something is being taken and divided.

loreStory.t: Gunnar
wears one wired in behind his belt buckle on the far rounds, through country the
Duskfang
still holds. Asked at the meadow fire what carrying it is like, he gave the question thought — which from Gunnar is a long answer already — and said: like being lent to. He did not say by whom.

items.name: Soulstone
items.description: Grey stone veined in dead violet, off a Gravecharger. It is still trying to reach a line that fell centuries ago.

soul.power: Charging attacks hit for +25% and knock the target back

items.loreDesc: Grey stone veined in dead violet, off a Gravecharger. It is still trying to reach a line that fell centuries ago.
loreStory: It pays nothing to a man standing still. Set into a spear-shaft or a shoulder-plate it adds a quarter to whatever you were already committed to, and it adds it at the far end of the movement, once you have run out of ways to change your mind. Setters keep it out of knives, a knife being a stopping weapon and this being no sort of stopping stone. People who wear one arrive at the far side of things they had meant to go around.

loreStory.t: The war
the horse
comes out of is in no book, and
Bettany

has spent a whole circuit of fires establishing that it is in nobody's mouth either. What she has instead is ninety-two gold on a bench: grey plates, dead violet in the seams, a pale star at the middle. A stone is one fact pressed down until it is nearly a mineral, and the fact in this one is not running, and is not fear, and is not carrying a man. It is a shape. The middle of a row, at a flat gallop, without checking. Which means there were rows, and somebody stood men in them, and worked an animal at them morning after morning until that was the last thing left in it.

loreStory: So it is a document, the shortest she owns, and the only source in the Chronicle she can verify by picking it up. What buyers pay for is the second half of the effect, the part where whatever you hit goes backwards. None of that is the animal's. That is what a line looks like from the front.

items.name: Soulstone
items.description: Black and webbed with hollow cracks, the dark that wore Grinmask's smile. Its cuts carry shadow straight through armor.

soul.power: +14 shadow damage on hit and ignores 10% of enemy armor

items.loreDesc: Cracked all the way through, with nothing in the cracks. What reached the bottom of this one was never its own.

loreStory.t: A soulstone is the bottom of a creature: one fact, one appetite, pressed to mineral. This one comes out of
Grinmask

cracked all the way through, and there is nothing in the cracks. Not damage — they all come out like that. The trade's working explanation is short and unpleasant: that shape was emptied long before anyone broke it, so what settled to the bottom of it was never the creature's own. It was the visitor's.
By that reading, everyone who carries one is carrying a fragment of
the thing under the mountain
. Several people have pointed this out. Nobody has stopped. The exception is
Hearn
, who has been nearer the source than anyone: he sold his the same evening it was paid to him, under its price, to a buyer he did not look at.

items.name: Soulstone
items.description: A mosaic that changes colour every time you look away, cut from a Prismclaw. Light bends around it.

soul.power: Attacks refract: +10% critical chance, and criticals strike a second time for half

items.loreDesc: A mosaic that changes colour every time you look away, off a Prismclaw. It lies a hand's width from where it looks.

loreStory.t: Appraisers pick this one up with their eyes shut, and there is no trick to it beyond knowing there is one. Light comes off the mosaic bent, so the stone is never quite where the cloth says it is, and a confident hand closes on nothing. Dealers' children learn it as a party piece years before they learn prices. The offset is always to the same side, which is the whole of the item: carry one a day and you are reaching a finger's width off for your own cup without having decided to. In a fight the good hit arrives, and then arrives again, half as hard, beside itself. Hunters in
that country
are taught before anything else to aim beside what they can see.

loreStory: Tap one and it gives a single high note, the same note off every stone of the kind, and any smith will tell you what that note means in a piece of steel: a flaw running the whole way through, an edge that is going to let go, and the only question left is which stroke. Nothing of the sort has ever happened. They do not chip and they do not part. It is a lie the stone has apparently always told, and it is also the fastest way to sort one from the leavings — out in the crystal country there are smooth boulders with snapped points scattered round the base, and people gather them up and sell them along the road as chips of the real thing, four gold, most of them honestly enough. Tapped, the points say nothing at all. They came off an animal trying to rub off something that was itself.

items.name: Soulstone
items.description: Black stone flooded with slow orange veins, quenched out of a Slagfang. Still too warm to pocket.

soul.power: +13 fire damage on hit, and your own wounds cauterize: no bleeding

items.loreDesc: Black stone flooded with slow orange veins, quenched out of a Slagfang. Still too warm to pocket.
loreStory: You cannot pocket one. Every new collector tries it once and buys a tin the same afternoon, and every bag that has worked the burnt country has a scorch inside where somebody learned. It does not cool. Held bare it sits at the limit of what a hand will agree to, and the trade's word for that is the honest one: quenched, not burning. Nothing runs out of it and nothing gets in.

It does the same for a fighter. Wounds shut as fast as they open; you do not bleed with one on you. A wolf that went into a caldera and came out with the seams standing open in its hide lost nothing through them either, and that flat fact is the whole of what reached the bottom.

loreStory.t: Every one of these ever brought in came down out of the east. Not most — every one, off a country
Solveig

has never walked and does not intend to. She has met nine of them at the other end of it, in the grass, when they are still only wet animals that cannot stand, and every one of them left her going the same way.

So she buys. Anyone coming down out of the burnt country with a stone gets the asking price without haggling, and inside the week she sells it on for exactly that, losing nothing, gaining nothing. What she keeps is the few days between: a warm thing in a cloth by her fire that has been where they were going.
The wolf
need not be one of hers. She knows that. She holds it anyway.

items.name: Soulstone
items.description: Mottled swamp-green, all a Mirewart leaves behind. Keep it near and small hurts seal themselves while you walk.

soul.power: +3 health regeneration per second

items.loreDesc: Mottled olive crust over smooth grey, dark in the seams. A Mirewart's last piece; small hurts close as you walk.
loreStory: The commonest stone there is: dealers do not count them, they weigh them, and a bagful has bought a first winter's boots for a great many people who came to the fires with nothing else to sell. The trade calls it a walking stone — it works between places and never during. Carry one across a long day and there is no moment you feel it; at the fire, the day's small hurts have closed without ceremony.

loreStory.t: The part worth more thought is who keeps them. A great many people are still carrying the first one they ever took, years past affording better, and
Bettany
has been collecting their reasons for
the Chronicle

: it is lucky, it is paid for, it sits right in a pocket. She notes that not one reason quite holds, and that every keeper can still say exactly where the water was and how the light sat on it. The first thing a frightened newcomer breaks in this country is very often
a slow green weight
that did not run, and what they carry up from the mud is this. Kept, she has written, the way an apology is kept by people who would rather carry it than say it.

items.name: Soulstone
items.description: Matte black and light-swallowing, an Ashfiend burnt down to this. It strikes with shadow and can hide you after a kill.
